Reconstructed mound in Shindo Otsukayama Park }} '''{{ill|Shindo Otsukayama Kofun|ja|真土大塚山古墳}}''' was an ancient burial mound located in '''{{ill|Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|ja|平塚市}}, Japan'''. The site is '''now lost''', but artifacts from the burial have been designated as an '''Important Cultural Property of Hiratsuka City'''. The original shape of the tumulus is debated, with '''three competing theories''': 1. '''{{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}} (double middle-round tumulus)''' 2. '''{{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} (keyhole-shaped tumulus)''' 3. '''{{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳}} (rectangular-front tumulus)''' However, '''no excavation was conducted before the mound was destroyed''', making its true form uncertain. == Discovery and Excavation == On '''March 18, 1935''', a '''local resident''' discovered a '''mirror, bronze arrowheads, a bronze bell, and iron swords''' while digging up tree roots. A '''field survey''' was conducted on '''March 20''', followed by a full '''excavation and mapping of the tumulus in January 1936'''. In '''1960''', another '''excavation and mapping''' took place, leading to new interpretations of the kofun's shape. In '''2016''', a '''re-evaluation''' suggested that it may have been a '''{{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}}'''. Today, a '''reconstructed mound''' is preserved '''inside Shindo Otsukayama Park'''. == Location == Shindo Otsukayama Kofun was built on a '''sand dune ridge''' along '''{{ill|Sagami Bay|ja|相模湾}}'''. At the time of excavation, the tumulus sat '''19.5 meters above sea level''', '''11 meters higher than nearby rice fields''', making it the '''highest point in the surrounding lowland'''. Because it was '''built on sand dunes''', early researchers '''nicknamed it "the sand dune tumulus"'''. The surrounding land was '''not highly fertile''', and no large settlements were found nearby. However, the kofun’s '''strategic location''' near both '''Sagami Bay''' and the '''Sagami River mouth''' suggests that it was constructed as a '''major landmark on a transportation route'''. == Structure == The mound was '''never fully excavated''', and its '''exact shape remains unknown'''. Based on surveys, three different hypotheses have been proposed: 1. '''Keyhole-shaped tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}}) 2. '''Rectangular-front tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳}}) 3. '''Double middle-round tumulus''' ({{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}}) Since the mound was destroyed before its '''structure could be confirmed''', the exact shape will never be known. ### '''Surface Features''' * '''Stone covering (Fuki-ishi)''' * A '''1960 excavation''' discovered '''fist-sized stones''' at the mound’s summit, suggesting a stone covering may have existed. * However, '''1936 excavation records make no mention of it''', making this uncertain. * '''Stepped construction (Dan-chiku)''' * No evidence was found. * '''Haniwa (ceramic tomb markers)''' * None were discovered. * '''Moat (Shuchu-kyokusen)''' * No moat was found. The '''burial chambers''' were located '''0.75–0.8 meters underground''' for the '''clay chamber burial''', and '''1.3 meters underground''' for the '''wooden coffin burial'''. == Artifacts == [[File:真土大塚山古墳出土 三角縁四神二獣鏡 (J-23148).JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Sankakuen Shijin Nijukyo mirror}}{{small|On display at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}.}}]] Artifacts from '''both burials''' include: ### '''Wooden Coffin Burial''' Discovered '''before World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}''': * '''1 {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror)''' - '''Identical to a mirror''' found in the '''{{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳}}''' (Kyoto), indicating a connection to '''the Yamato region'''. * '''Multiple {{ill|Kudatama|ja|管玉}} (tube beads) and circular bronze ornaments''' * '''39 bronze arrowheads''' * '''2 iron axes''' * '''1 sword fragment''' * '''1 knife fragment''' * '''Pottery fragments''' - Believed to date from the '''late Yayoi period''' to the '''early Kofun period'''. ### '''Clay Chamber Burial''' Excavated '''after World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Hiratsuka City Museum|ja|平塚市博物館}}''': * '''1 Four Beast Mirror (変形四獣鏡)''' * '''1 Crystal Magatama bead''' * '''2 Crystal "abacus" beads''' * '''150 glass beads''' * '''1 bronze arrowhead''' * '''3 bronze bells''' * '''1 spear-plane (槍鉋, yari-ganna)''' * '''Pottery fragments''' - Dated to the '''late Yayoi period''' or '''early Kofun period'''. {{Infobox Kofun | name = Shindo Otsukayama Kofun | native_name = 真土大塚山古墳 | location = {{ill|Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|ja|平塚市}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県}}, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|35|21|31.4|N|139|20|54.8|E|display=inline,title}} | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}} / {{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} / {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳}} | length = Unknown | built = Late 3rd century - Mid 4th century (or late 4th century) | burial = Wooden coffin burial, {{ill|Nendo-kaku|ja|粘土槨}} (clay chamber) | artifacts = {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror), weapons, jewelry | designated = None | map = Japan Kanagawa | map_caption = Location in Kanagawa Prefecture | image = [[File:Shindo Otsukayama Kofun, funkyu.jpg|280px]]
Reconstructed mound in Shindo Otsukayama Park }} '''{{ill|Shindo Otsukayama Kofun|ja|真土大塚山古墳}}''' was an ancient burial mound located in '''{{ill|Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|ja|平塚市}}, Japan'''. The site is '''now lost''', but artifacts from the burial have been designated as an '''Important Cultural Property of Hiratsuka City'''. The original shape of the tumulus is debated, with '''three competing theories''': 1. '''{{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}} (double middle-round tumulus)''' 2. '''{{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} (keyhole-shaped tumulus)''' 3. '''{{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳}} (rectangular-front tumulus)''' However, '''no excavation was conducted before the mound was destroyed''', making its true form uncertain. == Discovery and Excavation == On '''March 18, 1935''', a '''local resident''' discovered a '''mirror, bronze arrowheads, a bronze bell, and iron swords''' while digging up tree roots. A '''field survey''' was conducted on '''March 20''', followed by a full '''excavation and mapping of the tumulus in January 1936'''. In '''1960''', another '''excavation and mapping''' took place, leading to new interpretations of the kofun's shape. In '''2016''', a '''re-evaluation''' suggested that it may have been a '''{{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}}'''. Today, a '''reconstructed mound''' is preserved '''inside Shindo Otsukayama Park'''. == Location == Shindo Otsukayama Kofun was built on a '''sand dune ridge''' along '''{{ill|Sagami Bay|ja|相模湾}}'''. At the time of excavation, the tumulus sat '''19.5 meters above sea level''', '''11 meters higher than nearby rice fields''', making it the '''highest point in the surrounding lowland'''. Because it was '''built on sand dunes''', early researchers '''nicknamed it "the sand dune tumulus"'''. The surrounding land was '''not highly fertile''', and no large settlements were found nearby. However, the kofun’s '''strategic location''' near both '''Sagami Bay''' and the '''Sagami River mouth''' suggests that it was constructed as a '''major landmark on a transportation route'''. == Structure == The mound was '''never fully excavated''', and its '''exact shape remains unknown'''. Based on surveys, three different hypotheses have been proposed: 1. '''Keyhole-shaped tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}}) 2. '''Rectangular-front tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳}}) 3. '''Double middle-round tumulus''' ({{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}}) Since the mound was destroyed before its '''structure could be confirmed''', the exact shape will never be known. ### '''Surface Features''' * '''Stone covering (Fuki-ishi)''' * A '''1960 excavation''' discovered '''fist-sized stones''' at the mound’s summit, suggesting a stone covering may have existed. * However, '''1936 excavation records make no mention of it''', making this uncertain. * '''Stepped construction (Dan-chiku)''' * No evidence was found. * '''Haniwa (ceramic tomb markers)''' * None were discovered. * '''Moat (Shuchu-kyokusen)''' * No moat was found. The '''burial chambers''' were located '''0.75–0.8 meters underground''' for the '''clay chamber burial''', and '''1.3 meters underground''' for the '''wooden coffin burial'''. == Artifacts == [[File:真土大塚山古墳出土 三角縁四神二獣鏡 (J-23148).JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Sankakuen Shijin Nijukyo mirror}}{{small|On display at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}.}}]] Artifacts from '''both burials''' include: ### '''Wooden Coffin Burial''' Discovered '''before World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}''': * '''1 {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror)''' - '''Identical to a mirror''' found in the '''{{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳}}''' (Kyoto), indicating a connection to '''the Yamato region'''. * '''Multiple {{ill|Kudatama|ja|管玉}} (tube beads) and circular bronze ornaments''' * '''39 bronze arrowheads''' * '''2 iron axes''' * '''1 sword fragment''' * '''1 knife fragment''' * '''Pottery fragments''' - Believed to date from the '''late Yayoi period''' to the '''early Kofun period'''. ### '''Clay Chamber Burial''' Excavated '''after World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Hiratsuka City Museum|ja|平塚市博物館}}''': * '''1 Four Beast Mirror (変形四獣鏡)''' * '''1 Crystal Magatama bead''' * '''2 Crystal "abacus" beads''' * '''150 glass beads''' * '''1 bronze arrowhead''' * '''3 bronze bells''' * '''1 spear-plane (槍鉋, yari-ganna)''' * '''Pottery fragments''' - Dated to the '''late Yayoi period''' or '''early Kofun period'''. File:真土大塚山古墳出土 銅鏃.JPG|Bronze arrowheads
{{small|On display at the Matsudo City Museum.}} == Historical Significance == Although the mound itself '''was lost''', artifacts confirm that the person buried here had '''strong ties to the Yamato court'''. The kofun was likely built between the '''late 3rd century and mid-4th century''', or possibly in the '''late 4th century'''. It fills a '''chronological gap''' between the '''{{ill|Akibayama Kofun Cluster|ja|秋葉山古墳群}}''' and the '''{{ill|Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|ja|長柄桜山古墳群}}'''. Its '''location near the Sagami River''' suggests a '''close connection to marine trade routes''', particularly with the '''Nagara Sakurayama Kofun Group'''. Some scholars believe the tumulus was built by '''the Sōbu Kuni no Miyatsuko (相武国造)''', while others argue that the '''Shinaga Kuni no Miyatsuko (師長国造)''' controlled this region.[https://www.hirahaku.jp/hakubutsukan_archive/kouko/00000035/2.html Hiratsuka City Museum] == Cultural Properties == === '''Hiratsuka City Designated Cultural Property''' === * '''Important Cultural Property (Tangible Cultural Property)''' - "Shindo Otsukayama Kofun Excavated Artifacts" (designated February 1, 2010).[http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/bunka/page-c_01316.html Hiratsuka City Cultural Property Database] == External Links == * [http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/zukan/iseki/iseki_03.htm Hiratsuka City Archaeological Records] * {{Infobox Kofun | name = Shindo Otsukayama Kofun | native_name = 真土大塚山古墳 | location = {{ill|Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|ja|平塚市}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県}}, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|35|21|31.4|N|139|20|54.8|E|display=inline,title}} | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}} / {{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} / {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳}} | length = Unknown | built = Late 3rd century - Mid 4th century (or late 4th century) | burial = Wooden coffin burial, {{ill|Nendo-kaku|ja|粘土槨}} (clay chamber) | artifacts = {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror), weapons, jewelry | designated = None | map = Japan Kanagawa | map_caption = Location in Kanagawa Prefecture | image = [[File:Shindo Otsukayama Kofun, funkyu.jpg|280px]]
Reconstructed mound in Shindo Otsukayama Park }} '''{{ill|Shindo Otsukayama Kofun|ja|真土大塚山古墳}}''' was an ancient burial mound located in '''{{ill|Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|ja|平塚市}}, Japan'''. The site is '''now lost''', but artifacts from the burial have been designated as an '''Important Cultural Property of Hiratsuka City'''. The original shape of the tumulus is debated, with '''three competing theories''': 1. '''{{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}} (double middle-round tumulus)''' 2. '''{{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} (keyhole-shaped tumulus)''' 3. '''{{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳}} (rectangular-front tumulus)''' However, '''no excavation was conducted before the mound was destroyed''', making its true form uncertain. == Discovery and Excavation == On '''March 18, 1935''', a '''local resident''' discovered a '''mirror, bronze arrowheads, a bronze bell, and iron swords''' while digging up tree roots. A '''field survey''' was conducted on '''March 20''', followed by a full '''excavation and mapping of the tumulus in January 1936'''. In '''1960''', another '''excavation and mapping''' took place, leading to new interpretations of the kofun's shape. In '''2016''', a '''re-evaluation''' suggested that it may have been a '''{{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}}'''. Today, a '''reconstructed mound''' is preserved '''inside Shindo Otsukayama Park'''. == Location == Shindo Otsukayama Kofun was built on a '''sand dune ridge''' along '''{{ill|Sagami Bay|ja|相模湾}}'''. At the time of excavation, the tumulus sat '''19.5 meters above sea level''', '''11 meters higher than nearby rice fields''', making it the '''highest point in the surrounding lowland'''. Because it was '''built on sand dunes''', early researchers '''nicknamed it "the sand dune tumulus"'''. The surrounding land was '''not highly fertile''', and no large settlements were found nearby. However, the kofun’s '''strategic location''' near both '''Sagami Bay''' and the '''Sagami River mouth''' suggests that it was constructed as a '''major landmark on a transportation route'''. == Structure == The mound was '''never fully excavated''', and its '''exact shape remains unknown'''. Based on surveys, three different hypotheses have been proposed: 1. '''Keyhole-shaped tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}}) 2. '''Rectangular-front tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳}}) 3. '''Double middle-round tumulus''' ({{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}}) Since the mound was destroyed before its '''structure could be confirmed''', the exact shape will never be known. ### '''Surface Features''' * '''Stone covering (Fuki-ishi)''' * A '''1960 excavation''' discovered '''fist-sized stones''' at the mound’s summit, suggesting a stone covering may have existed. * However, '''1936 excavation records make no mention of it''', making this uncertain. * '''Stepped construction (Dan-chiku)''' * No evidence was found. * '''Haniwa (ceramic tomb markers)''' * None were discovered. * '''Moat (Shuchu-kyokusen)''' * No moat was found. The '''burial chambers''' were located '''0.75–0.8 meters underground''' for the '''clay chamber burial''', and '''1.3 meters underground''' for the '''wooden coffin burial'''. == Artifacts == [[File:真土大塚山古墳出土 三角縁四神二獣鏡 (J-23148).JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Sankakuen Shijin Nijukyo mirror}}{{small|On display at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}.}}]] Artifacts from '''both burials''' include: ### '''Wooden Coffin Burial''' Discovered '''before World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}''': * '''1 {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror)''' - '''Identical to a mirror''' found in the '''{{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳}}''' (Kyoto), indicating a connection to '''the Yamato region'''. * '''Multiple {{ill|Kudatama|ja|管玉}} (tube beads) and circular bronze ornaments''' * '''39 bronze arrowheads''' * '''2 iron axes''' * '''1 sword fragment''' * '''1 knife fragment''' * '''Pottery fragments''' - Believed to date from the '''late Yayoi period''' to the '''early Kofun period'''. ### '''Clay Chamber Burial''' Excavated '''after World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Hiratsuka City Museum|ja|平塚市博物館}}''': * '''1 Four Beast Mirror (変形四獣鏡)''' * '''1 Crystal Magatama bead''' * '''2 Crystal "abacus" beads''' * '''150 glass beads''' * '''1 bronze arrowhead''' * '''3 bronze bells''' * '''1 spear-plane (槍鉋, yari-ganna)''' * '''Pottery fragments''' - Dated to the '''late Yayoi period''' or '''early Kofun period'''. File:真土大塚山古墳出土 銅鏃.JPG|Bronze arrowheads
{{small|On display at the Matsudo City Museum.}} == Historical Significance == Although the mound itself '''was lost''', artifacts confirm that the person buried here had '''strong ties to the Yamato court'''. The kofun was likely built between the '''late 3rd century and mid-4th century''', or possibly in the '''late 4th century'''. It fills a '''chronological gap''' between the '''{{ill|Akibayama Kofun Cluster|ja|秋葉山古墳群}}''' and the '''{{ill|Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|ja|長柄桜山古墳群}}'''. Its '''location near the Sagami River''' suggests a '''close connection to marine trade routes''', particularly with the '''Nagara Sakurayama Kofun Group'''. Some scholars believe the tumulus was built by '''the Sōbu Kuni no Miyatsuko (相武国造)''', while others argue that the '''Shinaga Kuni no Miyatsuko (師長国造)''' controlled this region.[https://www.hirahaku.jp/hakubutsukan_archive/kouko/00000035/2.html Hiratsuka City Museum] == Cultural Properties == === '''Hiratsuka City Designated Cultural Property''' === * '''Important Cultural Property (Tangible Cultural Property)''' - "Shindo Otsukayama Kofun Excavated Artifacts" (designated February 1, 2010).[http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/bunka/page-c_01316.html Hiratsuka City Cultural Property Database] == External Links == * [http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/zukan/iseki/iseki_03.htm Hiratsuka City Archaeological Records] * Based on surveys, three different hypotheses have been proposed: 1. '''Keyhole-shaped tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}}) 2. '''Rectangular-front tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳}}) 3. '''Double middle-round tumulus''' ({{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}}) Since the mound was destroyed before its '''structure could be confirmed''', the exact shape will never be known. ### '''Surface Features''' * '''Stone covering (Fuki-ishi)''' * A '''1960 excavation''' discovered '''fist-sized stones''' at the mound’s summit, suggesting a stone covering may have existed. * However, '''1936 excavation records make no mention of it''', making this uncertain. * '''Stepped construction (Dan-chiku)''' * No evidence was found. * '''Haniwa (ceramic tomb markers)''' * None were discovered. * '''Moat (Shuchu-kyokusen)''' * No moat was found. The '''burial chambers''' were located '''0.75–0.8 meters underground''' for the '''clay chamber burial''', and '''1.3 meters underground''' for the '''wooden coffin burial'''. == Artifacts == [[File:真土大塚山古墳出土 三角縁四神二獣鏡 (J-23148).JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Sankakuen Shijin Nijukyo mirror}}{{small|On display at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}.}}]] Artifacts from '''both burials''' include: ### '''Wooden Coffin Burial''' Discovered '''before World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}''': * '''1 {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror)''' - '''Identical to a mirror''' found in the '''{{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳}}''' (Kyoto), indicating a connection to '''the Yamato region'''. * '''Multiple {{ill|Kudatama|ja|管玉}} (tube beads) and circular bronze ornaments''' * '''39 bronze arrowheads''' * '''2 iron axes''' * '''1 sword fragment''' * '''1 knife fragment''' * '''Pottery fragments''' - Believed to date from the '''late Yayoi period''' to the '''early Kofun period'''. ### '''Clay Chamber Burial''' Excavated '''after World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Hiratsuka City Museum|ja|平塚市博物館}}''': * '''1 Four Beast Mirror (変形四獣鏡)''' * '''1 Crystal Magatama bead''' * '''2 Crystal "abacus" beads''' * '''150 glass beads''' * '''1 bronze arrowhead''' * '''3 bronze bells''' * '''1 spear-plane (槍鉋, yari-ganna)''' * '''Pottery fragments''' - Dated to the '''late Yayoi period''' or '''early Kofun period'''. File:真土大塚山古墳出土 銅鏃.JPG|Bronze arrowheads
{{small|On display at the Matsudo City Museum.}} == Historical Significance == Although the mound itself '''was lost''', artifacts confirm that the person buried here had '''strong ties to the Yamato court'''. The kofun was likely built between the '''late 3rd century and mid-4th century''', or possibly in the '''late 4th century'''. It fills a '''chronological gap''' between the '''{{ill|Akibayama Kofun Cluster|ja|秋葉山古墳群}}''' and the '''{{ill|Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|ja|長柄桜山古墳群}}'''. Its '''location near the Sagami River''' suggests a '''close connection to marine trade routes''', particularly with the '''Nagara Sakurayama Kofun Group'''. Some scholars believe the tumulus was built by '''the Sōbu Kuni no Miyatsuko (相武国造)''', while others argue that the '''Shinaga Kuni no Miyatsuko (師長国造)''' controlled this region.[https://www.hirahaku.jp/hakubutsukan_archive/kouko/00000035/2.html Hiratsuka City Museum] == Cultural Properties == === '''Hiratsuka City Designated Cultural Property''' === * '''Important Reconstructed mound in Shindo Otsukayama Park }} '''{{ill|Shindo Otsukayama Kofun|ja|真土大塚山古墳}}''' was an ancient burial mound located in '''{{ill|Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|ja|平塚市}}, Japan'''. The site is '''now lost''', but artifacts from the burial have been designated as an '''Important Cultural Property of Hiratsuka City'''. The original shape of the tumulus is debated, with '''three competing theories''': 1. '''{{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}} (double middle-round tumulus)''' 2. '''{{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} (keyhole-shaped tumulus)''' 3. '''{{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳}} (rectangular-front tumulus)''' However, '''no excavation was conducted before the mound was destroyed''', making its true form uncertain. == Discovery and Excavation == On '''March 18, 1935''', a '''local resident''' discovered a '''mirror, bronze arrowheads, a bronze bell, and iron swords''' while digging up tree roots. A '''field survey''' was conducted on '''March 20''', followed by a full '''excavation and mapping of the tumulus in January 1936'''. In '''1960''', another '''excavation and mapping''' took place, leading to new interpretations of the kofun's shape. In '''2016''', a '''re-evaluation''' suggested that it may have been a '''{{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}}'''. Today, a '''reconstructed mound''' is preserved '''inside Shindo Otsukayama Park'''. == Location == Shindo Otsukayama Kofun was built on a '''sand dune ridge''' along '''{{ill|Sagami Bay|ja|相模湾}}'''. At the time of excavation, the tumulus sat '''19.5 meters above sea level''', '''11 meters higher than nearby rice fields''', making it the '''highest point in the surrounding lowland'''. Because it was '''built on sand dunes''', early researchers '''nicknamed it "the sand dune tumulus"'''. The surrounding land was '''not highly fertile''', and no large settlements were found nearby. However, the kofun’s '''strategic location''' near both '''Sagami Bay''' and the '''Sagami River mouth''' suggests that it was constructed as a '''major landmark on a transportation route'''. == Structure == The mound was '''never fully excavated''', and its '''exact shape remains unknown'''. Based on surveys, three different hypotheses have been proposed: 1. '''Keyhole-shaped tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}}) 2. '''Rectangular-front tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳}}) 3. '''Double middle-round tumulus''' ({{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}}) Since the mound was destroyed before its '''structure could be confirmed''', the exact shape will never be known. ### '''Surface Features''' * '''Stone covering (Fuki-ishi)''' * A '''1960 excavation''' discovered '''fist-sized stones''' at the mound’s summit, suggesting a stone covering may have existed. * However, '''1936 excavation records make no mention of it''', making this uncertain. * '''Stepped construction (Dan-chiku)''' * No evidence was found. * '''Haniwa (ceramic tomb markers)''' * None were discovered. * '''Moat (Shuchu-kyokusen)''' * No moat was found. The '''burial chambers''' were located '''0.75–0.8 meters underground''' for the '''clay chamber burial''', and '''1.3 meters underground''' for the '''wooden coffin burial'''. == Artifacts == [[File:真土大塚山古墳出土 三角縁四神二獣鏡 (J-23148).JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Sankakuen Shijin Nijukyo mirror}}{{small|On display at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}.}}]] Artifacts from '''both burials''' include: ### '''Wooden Coffin Burial''' Discovered '''before World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}''': * '''1 {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror)''' - '''Identical to a mirror''' found in the '''{{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳}}''' (Kyoto), indicating a connection to '''the Yamato region'''. * '''Multiple {{ill|Kudatama|ja|管玉}} (tube beads) and circular bronze ornaments''' * '''39 bronze arrowheads''' * '''2 iron axes''' * '''1 sword fragment''' * '''1 knife fragment''' * '''Pottery fragments''' - Believed to date from the '''late Yayoi period''' to the '''early Kofun period'''. ### '''Clay Chamber Burial''' Excavated '''after World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Hiratsuka City Museum|ja|平塚市博物館}}''': * '''1 Four Beast Mirror (変形四獣鏡)''' * '''1 Crystal Magatama bead''' * '''2 Crystal "abacus" beads''' * '''150 glass beads''' * '''1 bronze arrowhead''' * '''3 bronze bells''' * '''1 spear-plane (槍鉋, yari-ganna)''' * '''Pottery fragments''' - Dated to the '''late Yayoi period''' or '''early Kofun period'''. It fills a '''chronological gap''' between the '''{{ill|Akibayama Kofun Cluster|ja|秋葉山古墳群}}''' and the '''{{ill|Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|ja|長柄桜山古墳群}}'''. {{Infobox Kofun | name = Shindo Otsukayama Kofun | native_name = 真土大塚山古墳 | location = {{ill|Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|ja|平塚市}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県}}, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|35|21|31.4|N|139|20|54.8|E|display=inline,title}} | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}} / {{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} / {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳}} | length = Unknown | built = Late 3rd century - Mid 4th century (or late 4th century) | burial = Wooden coffin burial, {{ill|Nendo-kaku|ja|粘土槨}} (clay chamber) | artifacts = {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror), weapons, jewelry | designated = None | map = Japan Kanagawa | map_caption = Location in Kanagawa Prefecture | image = [[File:Shindo Otsukayama Kofun, funkyu.jpg|280px]]
Reconstructed mound in Shindo Otsukayama Park }} '''{{ill|Shindo Otsukayama Kofun|ja|真土大塚山古墳}}''' was an ancient burial mound located in '''{{ill|Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|ja|平塚市}}, Japan'''. The site is '''now lost''', but artifacts from the burial have been designated as an '''Important Cultural Property of Hiratsuka City'''. The original shape of the tumulus is debated, with '''three competing theories''': 1. '''{{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}} (double middle-round tumulus)''' 2. '''{{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} (keyhole-shaped tumulus)''' 3. '''{{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳}} (rectangular-front tumulus)''' However, '''no excavation was conducted before the mound was destroyed''', making its true form uncertain. == Discovery and Excavation == On '''March 18, 1935''', a '''local resident''' discovered a '''mirror, bronze arrowheads, a bronze bell, and iron swords''' while digging up tree roots. A '''field survey''' was conducted on '''March 20''', followed by a full '''excavation and mapping of the tumulus in January 1936'''. In '''1960''', another '''excavation and mapping''' took place, leading to new interpretations of the kofun's shape. In '''2016''', a '''re-evaluation''' suggested that it may have been a '''{{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}}'''. Today, a '''reconstructed mound''' is preserved '''inside Shindo Otsukayama Park'''. == Location == Shindo Otsukayama Kofun was built on a '''sand dune ridge''' along '''{{ill|Sagami Bay|ja|相模湾}}'''. At the time of excavation, the tumulus sat '''19.5 meters above sea level''', '''11 meters higher than nearby rice fields''', making it the '''highest point in the surrounding lowland'''. Because it was '''built on sand dunes''', early researchers '''nicknamed it "the sand dune tumulus"'''. The surrounding land was '''not highly fertile''', and no large settlements were found nearby. However, the kofun’s '''strategic location''' near both '''Sagami Bay''' and the '''Sagami River mouth''' suggests that it was constructed as a '''major landmark on a transportation route'''. == Structure == The mound was '''never fully excavated''', and its '''exact shape remains unknown'''. Based on surveys, three different hypotheses have been proposed: 1. '''Keyhole-shaped tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}}) 2. '''Rectangular-front tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳}}) 3. '''Double middle-round tumulus''' ({{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}}) Since the mound was destroyed before its '''structure could be confirmed''', the exact shape will never be known. ### '''Surface Features''' * '''Stone covering (Fuki-ishi)''' * A '''1960 excavation''' discovered '''fist-sized stones''' at the mound’s summit, suggesting a stone covering may have existed. * However, '''1936 excavation records make no mention of it''', making this uncertain. * '''Stepped construction (Dan-chiku)''' * No evidence was found. * '''Haniwa (ceramic tomb markers)''' * None were discovered. * '''Moat (Shuchu-kyokusen)''' * No moat was found. The '''burial chambers''' were located '''0.75–0.8 meters underground''' for the '''clay chamber burial''', and '''1.3 meters underground''' for the '''wooden coffin burial'''. == Artifacts == [[File:真土大塚山古墳出土 三角縁四神二獣鏡 (J-23148).JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Sankakuen Shijin Nijukyo mirror}}{{small|On display at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}.}}]] Artifacts from '''both burials''' include: ### '''Wooden Coffin Burial''' Discovered '''before World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}''': * '''1 {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror)''' - '''Identical to a mirror''' found in the '''{{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳}}''' (Kyoto), indicating a connection to '''the Yamato region'''. * '''Multiple {{ill|Kudatama|ja|管玉}} (tube beads) and circular bronze ornaments''' * '''39 bronze arrowheads''' * '''2 iron axes''' * '''1 sword fragment''' * '''1 knife fragment''' * '''Pottery fragments''' - Believed to date from the '''late Yayoi period''' to the '''early Kofun period'''. ### '''Clay Chamber Burial''' Excavated '''after World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Hiratsuka City Museum|ja|平塚市博物館}}''': * '''1 Four Beast Mirror (変形四獣鏡)''' * '''1 Crystal Magatama bead''' * '''2 Crystal "abacus" beads''' * '''150 glass beads''' * '''1 bronze arrowhead''' * '''3 bronze bells''' * '''1 spear-plane (槍鉋, yari-ganna)''' * '''Pottery fragments''' - Dated to the '''late Yayoi period''' or '''early Kofun period'''. File:真土大塚山古墳出土 銅鏃.JPG|Bronze arrowheads
{{small|On display at the Matsudo City Museum.}} == Historical Significance == Although the mound itself '''was lost''', artifacts confirm that the person buried here had '''strong ties to the Yamato court'''. The kofun was likely built between the '''late 3rd century and mid-4th century''', or possibly in the '''late 4th century'''. It fills a '''chronological gap''' between the '''{{ill|Akibayama Kofun Cluster|ja|秋葉山古墳群}}''' and the '''{{ill|Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|ja|長柄桜山古墳群}}'''. Its '''location near the Sagami River''' suggests a '''close connection to marine trade routes''', particularly with the '''Nagara Sakurayama Kofun Group'''. Some scholars believe the tumulus was built by '''the Sōbu Kuni no Miyatsuko (相武国造)''', while others argue that the '''Shinaga Kuni no Miyatsuko (師長国造)''' controlled this region.[https://www.hirahaku.jp/hakubutsukan_archive/kouko/00000035/2.html Hiratsuka City Museum] == Cultural Properties == === '''Hiratsuka City Designated Cultural Property''' === * '''Important Cultural Property (Tangible Cultural Property)''' - "Shindo Otsukayama Kofun Excavated Artifacts" (designated February 1, 2010).[http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/bunka/page-c_01316.html Hiratsuka City Cultural Property Database] == External Links == * [http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/zukan/iseki/iseki_03.htm Hiratsuka City Archaeological Records] * revision.text:
{{Infobox Kofun | name = Shindo Otsukayama Kofun | native_name = 真土大塚山古墳 | location = {{ill|Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|ja|平塚市}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県}}, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|35|21|31.4|N|139|20|54.8|E|display=inline,title}} | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}} / {{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} / {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} | length = Unknown | built = Late 3rd century - Mid 4th century (or late 4th century) | burial = Wooden coffin burial, {{ill|Nendo-kaku|ja|粘土槨}} (clay chamber) | artifacts = {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror), weapons, jewelry | designated = None | map = Japan Kanagawa | map_caption = Location in Kanagawa Prefecture | image = [[File:Shindo Otsukayama Kofun, funkyu.jpg|280px]]
Reconstructed mound in Shindo Otsukayama Park }} '''{{ill|Shindo Otsukayama Kofun|ja|真土大塚山古墳}}''' was an ancient burial mound located in '''{{ill|Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|ja|平塚市}}, Japan'''. The site is '''now lost''', but artifacts from the burial have been designated as an '''Important Cultural Property of Hiratsuka City'''. The original shape of the tumulus is debated, with '''three competing theories''': 1. '''{{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}} (double middle-round tumulus)''' 2. '''{{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} (keyhole-shaped tumulus)''' 3. '''{{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} (rectangular-front tumulus)''' However, '''no excavation was conducted before the mound was destroyed''', making its true form uncertain. == Discovery and Excavation == On '''March 18, 1935''', a '''local resident''' discovered a '''mirror, bronze arrowheads, a bronze bell, and iron swords''' while digging up tree roots. A '''field survey''' was conducted on '''March 20''', followed by a full '''excavation and mapping of the tumulus in January 1936'''. In '''1960''', another '''excavation and mapping''' took place, leading to new interpretations of the kofun's shape. In '''2016''', a '''re-evaluation''' suggested that it may have been a '''{{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}}'''. Today, a '''reconstructed mound''' is preserved '''inside Shindo Otsukayama Park'''. == Location == Shindo Otsukayama Kofun was built on a '''sand dune ridge''' along '''{{ill|Sagami Bay|ja|相模湾}}'''. At the time of excavation, the tumulus sat '''19.5 meters above sea level''', '''11 meters higher than nearby rice fields''', making it the '''highest point in the surrounding lowland'''. Because it was '''built on sand dunes''', early researchers '''nicknamed it "the sand dune tumulus"'''. The surrounding land was '''not highly fertile''', and no large settlements were found nearby. However, the kofun’s '''strategic location''' near both '''Sagami Bay''' and the '''Sagami River mouth''' suggests that it was constructed as a '''major landmark on a transportation route'''. == Structure == The mound was '''never fully excavated''', and its '''exact shape remains unknown'''. Based on surveys, three different hypotheses have been proposed: 1. '''Keyhole-shaped tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}}) 2. '''Rectangular-front tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}}) 3. '''Double middle-round tumulus''' ({{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}}) Since the mound was destroyed before its '''structure could be confirmed''', the exact shape will never be known. ### '''Surface Features''' * '''Stone covering (Fuki-ishi)''' * A '''1960 excavation''' discovered '''fist-sized stones''' at the mound’s summit, suggesting a stone covering may have existed. * However, '''1936 excavation records make no mention of it''', making this uncertain. * '''Stepped construction (Dan-chiku)''' * No evidence was found. * '''Haniwa (ceramic tomb markers)''' * None were discovered. * '''Moat (Shuchu-kyokusen)''' * No moat was found. The '''burial chambers''' were located '''0.75–0.8 meters underground''' for the '''clay chamber burial''', and '''1.3 meters underground''' for the '''wooden coffin burial'''. == Artifacts == [[File:真土大塚山古墳出土 三角縁四神二獣鏡 (J-23148).JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Sankakuen Shijin Nijukyo mirror}}{{small|On display at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}.}}]] Artifacts from '''both burials''' include: ### '''Wooden Coffin Burial''' Discovered '''before World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}''': * '''1 {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror)''' - '''Identical to a mirror''' found in the '''{{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳}}''' (Kyoto), indicating a connection to '''the Yamato region'''. * '''Multiple {{ill|Kudatama|ja|管玉}} (tube beads) and circular bronze ornaments''' * '''39 bronze arrowheads''' * '''2 iron axes''' * '''1 sword fragment''' * '''1 knife fragment''' * '''Pottery fragments''' - Believed to date from the '''late Yayoi period''' to the '''early Kofun period'''. ### '''Clay Chamber Burial''' Excavated '''after World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Hiratsuka City Museum|ja|平塚市博物館}}''': * '''1 Four Beast Mirror (変形四獣鏡)''' * '''1 Crystal Magatama bead''' * '''2 Crystal "abacus" beads''' * '''150 glass beads''' * '''1 bronze arrowhead''' * '''3 bronze bells''' * '''1 spear-plane (槍鉋, yari-ganna)''' * '''Pottery fragments''' - Dated to the '''late Yayoi period''' or '''early Kofun period'''. File:真土大塚山古墳出土 銅鏃.JPG|Bronze arrowheads
{{small|On display at the Matsudo City Museum.}} == Historical Significance == Although the mound itself '''was lost''', artifacts confirm that the person buried here had '''strong ties to the Yamato court'''. The kofun was likely built between the '''late 3rd century and mid-4th century''', or possibly in the '''late 4th century'''. It fills a '''chronological gap''' between the '''{{ill|Akibayama Kofun Cluster|ja|秋葉山古墳群}}''' and the '''{{ill|Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|ja|長柄桜山古墳群}}'''. Its '''location near the Sagami River''' suggests a '''close connection to marine trade routes''', particularly with the '''Nagara Sakurayama Kofun Group'''. Some scholars believe the tumulus was built by '''the Sōbu Kuni no Miyatsuko (相武国造)''', while others argue that the '''Shinaga Kuni no Miyatsuko (師長国造)''' controlled this region.[https://www.hirahaku.jp/hakubutsukan_archive/kouko/00000035/2.html Hiratsuka City Museum] == Cultural Properties == === '''Hiratsuka City Designated Cultural Property''' === * '''Important Cultural Property (Tangible Cultural Property)''' - "Shindo Otsukayama Kofun Excavated Artifacts" (designated February 1, 2010).[http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/bunka/page-c_01316.html Hiratsuka City Cultural Property Database] == External Links == * [http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/zukan/iseki/iseki_03.htm Hiratsuka City Archaeological Records] * {{Infobox Kofun | name = Shindo Otsukayama Kofun | native_name = 真土大塚山古墳 | location = {{ill|Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|ja|平塚市}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県}}, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|35|21|31.4|N|139|20|54.8|E|display=inline,title}} | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}} / {{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} / {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} | length = Unknown | built = Late 3rd century - Mid 4th century (or late 4th century) | burial = Wooden coffin burial, {{ill|Nendo-kaku|ja|粘土槨}} (clay chamber) | artifacts = {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror), weapons, jewelry | designated = None | map = Japan Kanagawa | map_caption = Location in Kanagawa Prefecture | image = [[File:Shindo Otsukayama Kofun, funkyu.jpg|280px]]
Reconstructed mound in Shindo Otsukayama Park }} '''{{ill|Shindo Otsukayama Kofun|ja|真土大塚山古墳}}''' was an ancient burial mound located in '''{{ill|Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|ja|平塚市}}, Japan'''. The site is '''now lost''', but artifacts from the burial have been designated as an '''Important Cultural Property of Hiratsuka City'''. The original shape of the tumulus is debated, with '''three competing theories''': 1. '''{{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}} (double middle-round tumulus)''' 2. '''{{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} (keyhole-shaped tumulus)''' 3. '''{{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} (rectangular-front tumulus)''' However, '''no excavation was conducted before the mound was destroyed''', making its true form uncertain. == Discovery and Excavation == On '''March 18, 1935''', a '''local resident''' discovered a '''mirror, bronze arrowheads, a bronze bell, and iron swords''' while digging up tree roots. A '''field survey''' was conducted on '''March 20''', followed by a full '''excavation and mapping of the tumulus in January 1936'''. In '''1960''', another '''excavation and mapping''' took place, leading to new interpretations of the kofun's shape. In '''2016''', a '''re-evaluation''' suggested that it may have been a '''{{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}}'''. Today, a '''reconstructed mound''' is preserved '''inside Shindo Otsukayama Park'''. == Location == Shindo Otsukayama Kofun was built on a '''sand dune ridge''' along '''{{ill|Sagami Bay|ja|相模湾}}'''. At the time of excavation, the tumulus sat '''19.5 meters above sea level''', '''11 meters higher than nearby rice fields''', making it the '''highest point in the surrounding lowland'''. Because it was '''built on sand dunes''', early researchers '''nicknamed it "the sand dune tumulus"'''. The surrounding land was '''not highly fertile''', and no large settlements were found nearby. However, the kofun’s '''strategic location''' near both '''Sagami Bay''' and the '''Sagami River mouth''' suggests that it was constructed as a '''major landmark on a transportation route'''. == Structure == The mound was '''never fully excavated''', and its '''exact shape remains unknown'''. Based on surveys, three different hypotheses have been proposed: 1. '''Keyhole-shaped tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}}) 2. '''Rectangular-front tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}}) 3. '''Double middle-round tumulus''' ({{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}}) Since the mound was destroyed before its '''structure could be confirmed''', the exact shape will never be known. ### '''Surface Features''' * '''Stone covering (Fuki-ishi)''' * A '''1960 excavation''' discovered '''fist-sized stones''' at the mound’s summit, suggesting a stone covering may have existed. * However, '''1936 excavation records make no mention of it''', making this uncertain. * '''Stepped construction (Dan-chiku)''' * No evidence was found. * '''Haniwa (ceramic tomb markers)''' * None were discovered. * '''Moat (Shuchu-kyokusen)''' * No moat was found. The '''burial chambers''' were located '''0.75–0.8 meters underground''' for the '''clay chamber burial''', and '''1.3 meters underground''' for the '''wooden coffin burial'''. == Artifacts == [[File:真土大塚山古墳出土 三角縁四神二獣鏡 (J-23148).JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Sankakuen Shijin Nijukyo mirror}}{{small|On display at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}.}}]] Artifacts from '''both burials''' include: ### '''Wooden Coffin Burial''' Discovered '''before World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}''': * '''1 {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror)''' - '''Identical to a mirror''' found in the '''{{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳}}''' (Kyoto), indicating a connection to '''the Yamato region'''. * '''Multiple {{ill|Kudatama|ja|管玉}} (tube beads) and circular bronze ornaments''' * '''39 bronze arrowheads''' * '''2 iron axes''' * '''1 sword fragment''' * '''1 knife fragment''' * '''Pottery fragments''' - Believed to date from the '''late Yayoi period''' to the '''early Kofun period'''. ### '''Clay Chamber Burial''' Excavated '''after World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Hiratsuka City Museum|ja|平塚市博物館}}''': * '''1 Four Beast Mirror (変形四獣鏡)''' * '''1 Crystal Magatama bead''' * '''2 Crystal "abacus" beads''' * '''150 glass beads''' * '''1 bronze arrowhead''' * '''3 bronze bells''' * '''1 spear-plane (槍鉋, yari-ganna)''' * '''Pottery fragments''' - Dated to the '''late Yayoi period''' or '''early Kofun period'''. File:真土大塚山古墳出土 銅鏃.JPG|Bronze arrowheads
{{small|On display at the Matsudo City Museum.}} == Historical Significance == Although the mound itself '''was lost''', artifacts confirm that the person buried here had '''strong ties to the Yamato court'''. The kofun was likely built between the '''late 3rd century and mid-4th century''', or possibly in the '''late 4th century'''. It fills a '''chronological gap''' between the '''{{ill|Akibayama Kofun Cluster|ja|秋葉山古墳群}}''' and the '''{{ill|Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|ja|長柄桜山古墳群}}'''. Its '''location near the Sagami River''' suggests a '''close connection to marine trade routes''', particularly with the '''Nagara Sakurayama Kofun Group'''. Some scholars believe the tumulus was built by '''the Sōbu Kuni no Miyatsuko (相武国造)''', while others argue that the '''Shinaga Kuni no Miyatsuko (師長国造)''' controlled this region.[https://www.hirahaku.jp/hakubutsukan_archive/kouko/00000035/2.html Hiratsuka City Museum] == Cultural Properties == === '''Hiratsuka City Designated Cultural Property''' === * '''Important Cultural Property (Tangible Cultural Property)''' - "Shindo Otsukayama Kofun Excavated Artifacts" (designated February 1, 2010).[http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/bunka/page-c_01316.html Hiratsuka City Cultural Property Database] == External Links == * [http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/zukan/iseki/iseki_03.htm Hiratsuka City Archaeological Records] * {{Infobox Kofun | name = Shindo Otsukayama Kofun | native_name = 真土大塚山古墳 | location = {{ill|Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|ja|平塚市}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県}}, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|35|21|31.4|N|139|20|54.8|E|display=inline,title}} | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}} / {{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} / {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} | length = Unknown | built = Late 3rd century - Mid 4th century (or late 4th century) | burial = Wooden coffin burial, {{ill|Nendo-kaku|ja|粘土槨}} (clay chamber) | artifacts = {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror), weapons, jewelry | designated = None | map = Japan Kanagawa | map_caption = Location in Kanagawa Prefecture | image = [[File:Shindo Otsukayama Kofun, funkyu.jpg|280px]]
Reconstructed mound in Shindo Otsukayama Park }} '''{{ill|Shindo Otsukayama Kofun|ja|真土大塚山古墳}}''' was an ancient burial mound located in '''{{ill|Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|ja|平塚市}}, Japan'''. The site is '''now lost''', but artifacts from the burial have been designated as an '''Important Cultural Property of Hiratsuka City'''. The original shape of the tumulus is debated, with '''three competing theories''': 1. '''{{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}} (double middle-round tumulus)''' 2. '''{{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} (keyhole-shaped tumulus)''' 3. '''{{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} (rectangular-front tumulus)''' However, '''no excavation was conducted before the mound was destroyed''', making its true form uncertain. == Discovery and Excavation == On '''March 18, 1935''', a '''local resident''' discovered a '''mirror, bronze arrowheads, a bronze bell, and iron swords''' while digging up tree roots. A '''field survey''' was conducted on '''March 20''', followed by a full '''excavation and mapping of the tumulus in January 1936'''. In '''1960''', another '''excavation and mapping''' took place, leading to new interpretations of the kofun's shape. In '''2016''', a '''re-evaluation''' suggested that it may have been a '''{{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}}'''. Today, a '''reconstructed mound''' is preserved '''inside Shindo Otsukayama Park'''. == Location == Shindo Otsukayama Kofun was built on a '''sand dune ridge''' along '''{{ill|Sagami Bay|ja|相模湾}}'''. At the time of excavation, the tumulus sat '''19.5 meters above sea level''', '''11 meters higher than nearby rice fields''', making it the '''highest point in the surrounding lowland'''. Because it was '''built on sand dunes''', early researchers '''nicknamed it "the sand dune tumulus"'''. The surrounding land was '''not highly fertile''', and no large settlements were found nearby. However, the kofun’s '''strategic location''' near both '''Sagami Bay''' and the '''Sagami River mouth''' suggests that it was constructed as a '''major landmark on a transportation route'''. == Structure == The mound was '''never fully excavated''', and its '''exact shape remains unknown'''. Based on surveys, three different hypotheses have been proposed: 1. '''Keyhole-shaped tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}}) 2. '''Rectangular-front tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}}) 3. '''Double middle-round tumulus''' ({{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}}) Since the mound was destroyed before its '''structure could be confirmed''', the exact shape will never be known. ### '''Surface Features''' * '''Stone covering (Fuki-ishi)''' * A '''1960 excavation''' discovered '''fist-sized stones''' at the mound’s summit, suggesting a stone covering may have existed. * However, '''1936 excavation records make no mention of it''', making this uncertain. * '''Stepped construction (Dan-chiku)''' * No evidence was found. * '''Haniwa (ceramic tomb markers)''' * None were discovered. * '''Moat (Shuchu-kyokusen)''' * No moat was found. The '''burial chambers''' were located '''0.75–0.8 meters underground''' for the '''clay chamber burial''', and '''1.3 meters underground''' for the '''wooden coffin burial'''. == Artifacts == [[File:真土大塚山古墳出土 三角縁四神二獣鏡 (J-23148).JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Sankakuen Shijin Nijukyo mirror}}{{small|On display at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}.}}]] Artifacts from '''both burials''' include: ### '''Wooden Coffin Burial''' Discovered '''before World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}''': * '''1 {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror)''' - '''Identical to a mirror''' found in the '''{{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳}}''' (Kyoto), indicating a connection to '''the Yamato region'''. * '''Multiple {{ill|Kudatama|ja|管玉}} (tube beads) and circular bronze ornaments''' * '''39 bronze arrowheads''' * '''2 iron axes''' * '''1 sword fragment''' * '''1 knife fragment''' * '''Pottery fragments''' - Believed to date from the '''late Yayoi period''' to the '''early Kofun period'''. ### '''Clay Chamber Burial''' Excavated '''after World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Hiratsuka City Museum|ja|平塚市博物館}}''': * '''1 Four Beast Mirror (変形四獣鏡)''' * '''1 Crystal Magatama bead''' * '''2 Crystal "abacus" beads''' * '''150 glass beads''' * '''1 bronze arrowhead''' * '''3 bronze bells''' * '''1 spear-plane (槍鉋, yari-ganna)''' * '''Pottery fragments''' - Dated to the '''late Yayoi period''' or '''early Kofun period'''. File:真土大塚山古墳出土 銅鏃.JPG|Bronze arrowheads
{{small|On display at the Matsudo City Museum.}} == Historical Significance == Although the mound itself '''was lost''', artifacts confirm that the person buried here had '''strong ties to the Yamato court'''. The kofun was likely built between the '''late 3rd century and mid-4th century''', or possibly in the '''late 4th century'''. It fills a '''chronological gap''' between the '''{{ill|Akibayama Kofun Cluster|ja|秋葉山古墳群}}''' and the '''{{ill|Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|ja|長柄桜山古墳群}}'''. Its '''location near the Sagami River''' suggests a '''close connection to marine trade routes''', particularly with the '''Nagara Sakurayama Kofun Group'''. Some scholars believe the tumulus was built by '''the Sōbu Kuni no Miyatsuko (相武国造)''', while others argue that the '''Shinaga Kuni no Miyatsuko (師長国造)''' controlled this region.[https://www.hirahaku.jp/hakubutsukan_archive/kouko/00000035/2.html Hiratsuka City Museum] == Cultural Properties == === '''Hiratsuka City Designated Cultural Property''' === * '''Important Cultural Property (Tangible Cultural Property)''' - "Shindo Otsukayama Kofun Excavated Artifacts" (designated February 1, 2010).[http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/bunka/page-c_01316.html Hiratsuka City Cultural Property Database] == External Links == * [http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/zukan/iseki/iseki_03.htm Hiratsuka City Archaeological Records] * {{Infobox Kofun | name = Shindo Otsukayama Kofun | native_name = 真土大塚山古墳 | location = {{ill|Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|ja|平塚市}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県}}, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|35|21|31.4|N|139|20|54.8|E|display=inline,title}} | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}} / {{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} / {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} | length = Unknown | built = Late 3rd century - Mid 4th century (or late 4th century) | burial = Wooden coffin burial, {{ill|Nendo-kaku|ja|粘土槨}} (clay chamber) | artifacts = {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror), weapons, jewelry | designated = None | map = Japan Kanagawa | map_caption = Location in Kanagawa Prefecture | image = [[File:Shindo Otsukayama Kofun, funkyu.jpg|280px]]
Reconstructed mound in Shindo Otsukayama Park }} '''{{ill|Shindo Otsukayama Kofun|ja|真土大塚山古墳}}''' was an ancient burial mound located in '''{{ill|Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|ja|平塚市}}, Japan'''. The site is '''now lost''', but artifacts from the burial have been designated as an '''Important Cultural Property of Hiratsuka City'''. The original shape of the tumulus is debated, with '''three competing theories''': 1. '''{{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}} (double middle-round tumulus)''' 2. '''{{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} (keyhole-shaped tumulus)''' 3. '''{{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} (rectangular-front tumulus)''' However, '''no excavation was conducted before the mound was destroyed''', making its true form uncertain. == Discovery and Excavation == On '''March 18, 1935''', a '''local resident''' discovered a '''mirror, bronze arrowheads, a bronze bell, and iron swords''' while digging up tree roots. A '''field survey''' was conducted on '''March 20''', followed by a full '''excavation and mapping of the tumulus in January 1936'''. In '''1960''', another '''excavation and mapping''' took place, leading to new interpretations of the kofun's shape. In '''2016''', a '''re-evaluation''' suggested that it may have been a '''{{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}}'''. Today, a '''reconstructed mound''' is preserved '''inside Shindo Otsukayama Park'''. == Location == Shindo Otsukayama Kofun was built on a '''sand dune ridge''' along '''{{ill|Sagami Bay|ja|相模湾}}'''. At the time of excavation, the tumulus sat '''19.5 meters above sea level''', '''11 meters higher than nearby rice fields''', making it the '''highest point in the surrounding lowland'''. Because it was '''built on sand dunes''', early researchers '''nicknamed it "the sand dune tumulus"'''. The surrounding land was '''not highly fertile''', and no large settlements were found nearby. However, the kofun’s '''strategic location''' near both '''Sagami Bay''' and the '''Sagami River mouth''' suggests that it was constructed as a '''major landmark on a transportation route'''. == Structure == The mound was '''never fully excavated''', and its '''exact shape remains unknown'''. Based on surveys, three different hypotheses have been proposed: 1. '''Keyhole-shaped tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}}) 2. '''Rectangular-front tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}}) 3. '''Double middle-round tumulus''' ({{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}}) Since the mound was destroyed before its '''structure could be confirmed''', the exact shape will never be known. ### '''Surface Features''' * '''Stone covering (Fuki-ishi)''' * A '''1960 excavation''' discovered '''fist-sized stones''' at the mound’s summit, suggesting a stone covering may have existed. * However, '''1936 excavation records make no mention of it''', making this uncertain. * '''Stepped construction (Dan-chiku)''' * No evidence was found. * '''Haniwa (ceramic tomb markers)''' * None were discovered. * '''Moat (Shuchu-kyokusen)''' * No moat was found. The '''burial chambers''' were located '''0.75–0.8 meters underground''' for the '''clay chamber burial''', and '''1.3 meters underground''' for the '''wooden coffin burial'''. == Artifacts == [[File:真土大塚山古墳出土 三角縁四神二獣鏡 (J-23148).JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Sankakuen Shijin Nijukyo mirror}}{{small|On display at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}.}}]] Artifacts from '''both burials''' include: ### '''Wooden Coffin Burial''' Discovered '''before World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}''': * '''1 {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror)''' - '''Identical to a mirror''' found in the '''{{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳}}''' (Kyoto), indicating a connection to '''the Yamato region'''. * '''Multiple {{ill|Kudatama|ja|管玉}} (tube beads) and circular bronze ornaments''' * '''39 bronze arrowheads''' * '''2 iron axes''' * '''1 sword fragment''' * '''1 knife fragment''' * '''Pottery fragments''' - Believed to date from the '''late Yayoi period''' to the '''early Kofun period'''. ### '''Clay Chamber Burial''' Excavated '''after World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Hiratsuka City Museum|ja|平塚市博物館}}''': * '''1 Four Beast Mirror (変形四獣鏡)''' * '''1 Crystal Magatama bead''' * '''2 Crystal "abacus" beads''' * '''150 glass beads''' * '''1 bronze arrowhead''' * '''3 bronze bells''' * '''1 spear-plane (槍鉋, yari-ganna)''' * '''Pottery fragments''' - Dated to the '''late Yayoi period''' or '''early Kofun period'''. File:真土大塚山古墳出土 銅鏃.JPG|Bronze arrowheads
{{small|On display at the Matsudo City Museum.}} == Historical Significance == Although the mound itself '''was lost''', artifacts confirm that the person buried here had '''strong ties to the Yamato court'''. The kofun was likely built between the '''late 3rd century and mid-4th century''', or possibly in the '''late 4th century'''. It fills a '''chronological gap''' between the '''{{ill|Akibayama Kofun Cluster|ja|秋葉山古墳群}}''' and the '''{{ill|Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|ja|長柄桜山古墳群}}'''. Its '''location near the Sagami River''' suggests a '''close connection to marine trade routes''', particularly with the '''Nagara Sakurayama Kofun Group'''. Some scholars believe the tumulus was built by '''the Sōbu Kuni no Miyatsuko (相武国造)''', while others argue that the '''Shinaga Kuni no Miyatsuko (師長国造)''' controlled this region.[https://www.hirahaku.jp/hakubutsukan_archive/kouko/00000035/2.html Hiratsuka City Museum] == Cultural Properties == === '''Hiratsuka City Designated Cultural Property''' === * '''Important Cultural Property (Tangible Cultural Property)''' - "Shindo Otsukayama Kofun Excavated Artifacts" (designated February 1, 2010).[http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/bunka/page-c_01316.html Hiratsuka City Cultural Property Database] == External Links == * [http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/zukan/iseki/iseki_03.htm Hiratsuka City Archaeological Records] * revision.text:
{{Infobox Kofun | name = Shindo Otsukayama Kofun | native_name = 真土大塚山古墳 | location = {{ill|Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|ja|平塚市}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県}}, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|35|21|31.4|N|139|20|54.8|E|display=inline,title}} | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}} / {{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} / {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} | length = Unknown | built = Late 3rd century - Mid 4th century (or late 4th century) | burial = Wooden coffin burial, {{ill|Nendo-kaku|ja|粘土槨}} (clay chamber) | artifacts = {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror), weapons, jewelry | designated = None | map = Japan Kanagawa | map_caption = Location in Kanagawa Prefecture | image = [[File:Shindo Otsukayama Kofun, funkyu.jpg|280px]]
Reconstructed mound in Shindo Otsukayama Park }} '''{{ill|Shindo Otsukayama Kofun|ja|真土大塚山古墳}}''' was an ancient burial mound located in '''{{ill|Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|ja|平塚市}}, Japan'''. The site is '''now lost''', but artifacts from the burial have been designated as an '''Important Cultural Property of Hiratsuka City'''. The original shape of the tumulus is debated, with '''three competing theories''': 1. '''{{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}} (double middle-round tumulus)''' 2. '''{{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} (keyhole-shaped tumulus)''' 3. '''{{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} (rectangular-front tumulus)''' However, '''no excavation was conducted before the mound was destroyed''', making its true form uncertain. == Discovery and Excavation == On '''March 18, 1935''', a '''local resident''' discovered a '''mirror, bronze arrowheads, a bronze bell, and iron swords''' while digging up tree roots. A '''field survey''' was conducted on '''March 20''', followed by a full '''excavation and mapping of the tumulus in January 1936'''. In '''1960''', another '''excavation and mapping''' took place, leading to new interpretations of the kofun's shape. In '''2016''', a '''re-evaluation''' suggested that it may have been a '''{{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}}'''. Today, a '''reconstructed mound''' is preserved '''inside Shindo Otsukayama Park'''. == Location == Shindo Otsukayama Kofun was built on a '''sand dune ridge''' along '''{{ill|Sagami Bay|ja|相模湾}}'''. At the time of excavation, the tumulus sat '''19.5 meters above sea level''', '''11 meters higher than nearby rice fields''', making it the '''highest point in the surrounding lowland'''. Because it was '''built on sand dunes''', early researchers '''nicknamed it "the sand dune tumulus"'''. The surrounding land was '''not highly fertile''', and no large settlements were found nearby. However, the kofun’s '''strategic location''' near both '''Sagami Bay''' and the '''Sagami River mouth''' suggests that it was constructed as a '''major landmark on a transportation route'''. == Structure == The mound was '''never fully excavated''', and its '''exact shape remains unknown'''. Based on surveys, three different hypotheses have been proposed: 1. '''Keyhole-shaped tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}}) 2. '''Rectangular-front tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}}) 3. '''Double middle-round tumulus''' ({{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}}) Since the mound was destroyed before its '''structure could be confirmed''', the exact shape will never be known. ### '''Surface Features''' * '''Stone covering (Fuki-ishi)''' * A '''1960 excavation''' discovered '''fist-sized stones''' at the mound’s summit, suggesting a stone covering may have existed. * However, '''1936 excavation records make no mention of it''', making this uncertain. * '''Stepped construction (Dan-chiku)''' * No evidence was found. * '''Haniwa (ceramic tomb markers)''' * None were discovered. * '''Moat (Shuchu-kyokusen)''' * No moat was found. The '''burial chambers''' were located '''0.75–0.8 meters underground''' for the '''clay chamber burial''', and '''1.3 meters underground''' for the '''wooden coffin burial'''. == Artifacts == [[File:真土大塚山古墳出土 三角縁四神二獣鏡 (J-23148).JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Sankakuen Shijin Nijukyo mirror}}{{small|On display at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}.}}]] Artifacts from '''both burials''' include: ### '''Wooden Coffin Burial''' Discovered '''before World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}''': * '''1 {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror)''' - '''Identical to a mirror''' found in the '''{{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳}}''' (Kyoto), indicating a connection to '''the Yamato region'''. * '''Multiple {{ill|Kudatama|ja|管玉}} (tube beads) and circular bronze ornaments''' * '''39 bronze arrowheads''' * '''2 iron axes''' * '''1 sword fragment''' * '''1 knife fragment''' * '''Pottery fragments''' - Believed to date from the '''late Yayoi period''' to the '''early Kofun period'''. ### '''Clay Chamber Burial''' Excavated '''after World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Hiratsuka City Museum|ja|平塚市博物館}}''': * '''1 Four Beast Mirror (変形四獣鏡)''' * '''1 Crystal Magatama bead''' * '''2 Crystal "abacus" beads''' * '''150 glass beads''' * '''1 bronze arrowhead''' * '''3 bronze bells''' * '''1 spear-plane (槍鉋, yari-ganna)''' * '''Pottery fragments''' - Dated to the '''late Yayoi period''' or '''early Kofun period'''. File:真土大塚山古墳出土 銅鏃.JPG|Bronze arrowheads
{{small|On display at the Matsudo City Museum.}} == Historical Significance == Although the mound itself '''was lost''', artifacts confirm that the person buried here had '''strong ties to the Yamato court'''. The kofun was likely built between the '''late 3rd century and mid-4th century''', or possibly in the '''late 4th century'''. It fills a '''chronological gap''' between the '''{{ill|Akibayama Kofun Cluster|ja|秋葉山古墳群}}''' and the '''{{ill|Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|ja|長柄桜山古墳群}}'''. Its '''location near the Sagami River''' suggests a '''close connection to marine trade routes''', particularly with the '''Nagara Sakurayama Kofun Group'''. Some scholars believe the tumulus was built by '''the Sōbu Kuni no Miyatsuko (相武国造)''', while others argue that the '''Shinaga Kuni no Miyatsuko (師長国造)''' controlled this region.[https://www.hirahaku.jp/hakubutsukan_archive/kouko/00000035/2.html Hiratsuka City Museum] == Cultural Properties == === '''Hiratsuka City Designated Cultural Property''' === * '''Important Cultural Property (Tangible Cultural Property)''' - "Shindo Otsukayama Kofun Excavated Artifacts" (designated February 1, 2010).[http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/bunka/page-c_01316.html Hiratsuka City Cultural Property Database] == External Links == * [http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/zukan/iseki/iseki_03.htm Hiratsuka City Archaeological Records] * [http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/koen/page-c_02813.html Shindo Otsukayama Park] {{DEFAULTSORT:Shindo Otsukayama Kofun}} [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Kanagawa {{Infobox Kofun | name = Shindo Otsukayama Kofun | native_name = 真土大塚山古墳 | location = {{ill|Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|ja|平塚市}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県}}, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|35|21|31.4|N|139|20|54.8|E|display=inline,title}} | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}} / {{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} / {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} | length = Unknown | built = Late 3rd century - Mid 4th century (or late 4th century) | burial = Wooden coffin burial, {{ill|Nendo-kaku|ja|粘土槨}} (clay chamber) | artifacts = {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror), weapons, jewelry | designated = None | map = Japan Kanagawa | map_caption = Location in Kanagawa Prefecture | image = [[File:Shindo Otsukayama Kofun, funkyu.jpg|280px]]
Reconstructed mound in Shindo Otsukayama Park }} '''{{ill|Shindo Otsukayama Kofun|ja|真土大塚山古墳}}''' was an ancient burial mound located in '''{{ill|Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|ja|平塚市}}, Japan'''. The site is '''now lost''', but artifacts from the burial have been designated as an '''Important Cultural Property of Hiratsuka City'''. The original shape of the tumulus is debated, with '''three competing theories''': 1. '''{{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}} (double middle-round tumulus)''' 2. '''{{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}} (keyhole-shaped tumulus)''' 3. '''{{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}} (rectangular-front tumulus)''' However, '''no excavation was conducted before the mound was destroyed''', making its true form uncertain. == Discovery and Excavation == On '''March 18, 1935''', a '''local resident''' discovered a '''mirror, bronze arrowheads, a bronze bell, and iron swords''' while digging up tree roots. A '''field survey''' was conducted on '''March 20''', followed by a full '''excavation and mapping of the tumulus in January 1936'''. In '''1960''', another '''excavation and mapping''' took place, leading to new interpretations of the kofun's shape. In '''2016''', a '''re-evaluation''' suggested that it may have been a '''{{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}}'''. Today, a '''reconstructed mound''' is preserved '''inside Shindo Otsukayama Park'''. == Location == Shindo Otsukayama Kofun was built on a '''sand dune ridge''' along '''{{ill|Sagami Bay|ja|相模湾}}'''. At the time of excavation, the tumulus sat '''19.5 meters above sea level''', '''11 meters higher than nearby rice fields''', making it the '''highest point in the surrounding lowland'''. Because it was '''built on sand dunes''', early researchers '''nicknamed it "the sand dune tumulus"'''. The surrounding land was '''not highly fertile''', and no large settlements were found nearby. However, the kofun’s '''strategic location''' near both '''Sagami Bay''' and the '''Sagami River mouth''' suggests that it was constructed as a '''major landmark on a transportation route'''. == Structure == The mound was '''never fully excavated''', and its '''exact shape remains unknown'''. Based on surveys, three different hypotheses have been proposed: 1. '''Keyhole-shaped tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}}) 2. '''Rectangular-front tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun}}) 3. '''Double middle-round tumulus''' ({{ill|Soho-chuen-fun|ja|双方中円墳}}) Since the mound was destroyed before its '''structure could be confirmed''', the exact shape will never be known. ### '''Surface Features''' * '''Stone covering (Fuki-ishi)''' * A '''1960 excavation''' discovered '''fist-sized stones''' at the mound’s summit, suggesting a stone covering may have existed. * However, '''1936 excavation records make no mention of it''', making this uncertain. * '''Stepped construction (Dan-chiku)''' * No evidence was found. * '''Haniwa (ceramic tomb markers)''' * None were discovered. * '''Moat (Shuchu-kyokusen)''' * No moat was found. The '''burial chambers''' were located '''0.75–0.8 meters underground''' for the '''clay chamber burial''', and '''1.3 meters underground''' for the '''wooden coffin burial'''. == Artifacts == [[File:真土大塚山古墳出土 三角縁四神二獣鏡 (J-23148).JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Sankakuen Shijin Nijukyo mirror}}{{small|On display at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}.}}]] Artifacts from '''both burials''' include: ### '''Wooden Coffin Burial''' Discovered '''before World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館}}''': * '''1 {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror)''' - '''Identical to a mirror''' found in the '''{{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳}}''' (Kyoto), indicating a connection to '''the Yamato region'''. * '''Multiple {{ill|Kudatama|ja|管玉}} (tube beads) and circular bronze ornaments''' * '''39 bronze arrowheads''' * '''2 iron axes''' * '''1 sword fragment''' * '''1 knife fragment''' * '''Pottery fragments''' - Believed to date from the '''late Yayoi period''' to the '''early Kofun period'''. ### '''Clay Chamber Burial''' Excavated '''after World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Hiratsuka City Museum|ja|平塚市博物館}}''': * '''1 Four Beast Mirror (変形四獣鏡)''' * '''1 Crystal Magatama bead''' * '''2 Crystal "abacus" beads''' * '''150 glass beads''' * '''1 bronze arrowhead''' * '''3 bronze bells''' * '''1 spear-plane (槍鉋, yari-ganna)''' * '''Pottery fragments''' - Dated to the '''late Yayoi period''' or '''early Kofun period'''. File:真土大塚山古墳出土 銅鏃.JPG|Bronze arrowheads
{{small|On display at the Matsudo City Museum.}} == Historical Significance == Although the mound itself '''was lost''', artifacts confirm that the person buried here had '''strong ties to the Yamato court'''. The kofun was likely built between the '''late 3rd century and mid-4th century''', or possibly in the '''late 4th century'''. It fills a '''chronological gap''' between the '''{{ill|Akibayama Kofun Cluster|ja|秋葉山古墳群}}''' and the '''{{ill|Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|ja|長柄桜山古墳群}}'''. Its '''location near the Sagami River''' suggests a '''close connection to marine trade routes''', particularly with the '''Nagara Sakurayama Kofun Group'''. Some scholars believe the tumulus was built by '''the Sōbu Kuni no Miyatsuko (相武国造)''', while others argue that the '''Shinaga Kuni no Miyatsuko (師長国造)''' controlled this region.[https://www.hirahaku.jp/hakubutsukan_archive/kouko/00000035/2.html Hiratsuka City Museum] == Cultural Properties == === '''Hiratsuka City Designated Cultural Property''' === * '''Important Cultural Property (Tangible Cultural Property)''' - "Shindo Otsukayama Kofun Excavated Artifacts" (designated February 1, 2010).[http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/bunka/page-c_01316.html Hiratsuka City Cultural Property Database] == External Links == * [http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/zukan/iseki/iseki_03.htm Hiratsuka City Archaeological Records] *
