Reconstructed mound in Shindo Otsukayama Park }} '''{{ill|Shindo Otsukayama Kofun|ja|真土大塚山古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}''' was an ancient Kofun located in '''{{ill|Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|ja|平塚市|12=draft|12=draft}}, Japan'''. The site is '''now lost''', but burial goods from the burial have been designation1 as an '''Important Cultural Property of Hiratsuka City'''. The original type of the tumulus is debated, with '''three competing theories''': 1. '''{{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=draft|12=draft}} (double middle-round tumulus)''' 2. '''{{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}} (keyhole-shaped tumulus)''' 3. '''{{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft|12=draft}} (rectangular-front tumulus)''' However, '''no excavation was conducted before the mound was destroyed''', making its true form uncertain. == Discovery and Excavation == On '''March 18, 1935''', a '''local resident''' discovered a '''mirror, bronze arrowheads, a bronze bell, and iron swords''' while digging up tree roots. A '''field survey''' was conducted on '''March 20''', followed by a full '''excavation and mapping of the tumulus in January 1936'''. In '''1960''', another '''excavation and mapping''' took place, leading to new interpretations of the kofun's type. In '''2016''', a '''re-evaluation''' suggested that it may have been a '''{{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=draft|12=draft}}'''. Today, a '''reconstructed mound''' is preserved '''inside Shindo Otsukayama Park'''. == location == Shindo Otsukayama Kofun was built on a '''sand dune ridge''' along '''{{ill|Sagami Bay|ja|相模湾|12=draft|12=draft}}'''. At the time of excavation, the tumulus sat '''19.5 meters above sea level''', '''11 meters higher than nearby rice fields''', making it the '''highest point in the surrounding lowland'''. Because it was '''built on sand dunes''', early researchers '''nicknamed it "the sand dune tumulus"'''. The surrounding land was '''not highly fertile''', and no large settlements were found nearby. However, the kofun’s '''strategic location''' near both '''Sagami Bay''' and the '''Sagami River mouth''' suggests that it was constructed as a '''major landmark on a transportation route'''. == Structure == The mound was '''never fully excavated''', and its '''exact type remains unknown'''. Based on surveys, three different hypotheses have been proposed: 1. '''Keyhole-shaped tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}}) 2. '''Rectangular-front tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft|12=draft}}) 3. '''Double middle-round tumulus''' ({{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=draft|12=draft}}) Since the mound was destroyed before its '''structure could be confirmed''', the exact type will never be known. === === '''Surface Features''' === * '''Stone covering (Fuki-ishi)''' ** A '''1960 excavation''' discovered '''fist-sized stones''' at the mound’s summit, suggesting a stone covering may have existed. ** However, '''1936 excavation records make no mention of it''', making this uncertain. * '''Stepped construction (Dan-chiku)''' ** No evidence was found. * '''Haniwa (ceramic tomb markers)''' ** None were discovered. * '''Moat (Shuchu-kyokusen)''' ** No moat was found. The '''burial chambers''' were located '''0.75–0.8 meters underground''' for the '''clay chamber burial''', and '''1.3 meters underground''' for the '''wooden coffin burial'''. == burial goods == [[File:真土大塚山古墳出土 三角縁四神二獣鏡 (J-23148).JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Sankakuen Shijin Nijukyo mirror}}{{small|On display at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館|12=draft|12=draft}}.}}]] burial goods from '''both burials''' include: === === '''Wooden Coffin Burial''' === Discovered '''before World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館|12=draft|12=draft}}''': * '''1 {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡|1=Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|12=draft|12=draft}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror)''' ** '''Identical to a mirror''' found in the '''{{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}''' (Kyoto), indicating a connection to '''the Yamato region'''. * '''Multiple {{ill|Kudatama|ja|管玉|12=draft|12=draft}} (tube beads) and circular bronze ornaments''' * '''39 bronze arrowheads''' * '''2 iron axes''' * '''1 sword fragment''' * '''1 knife fragment''' * '''Pottery fragments''' ** Believed to date from the '''late Yayoi period''' to the '''early Kofun period'''. === === '''Clay Chamber Burial''' === Excavated '''after World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Hiratsuka City Museum|ja|平塚市博物館|12=draft|12=draft}}''': * '''1 Four Beast Mirror (変形四獣鏡)''' * '''1 Crystal Magatama bead''' * '''2 Crystal "abacus" beads''' * '''150 glass beads''' * '''1 bronze arrowhead''' * '''3 bronze bells''' * '''1 spear-plane (槍鉋, yari-ganna)''' * '''Pottery fragments''' ** Dated to the '''late Yayoi period''' or '''early Kofun period'''. File:真土大塚山古墳出土 銅鏃.JPG|Bronze arrowheads
{{small|On display at the Matsudo City Museum.}} == Historical Significance == Although the mound itself '''was lost''', burial goods confirm that the person buried here had '''strong ties to the Yamato court'''. The kofun was likely built between the '''late 3rd century and mid-4th century''', or possibly in the '''late 4th century'''. It fills a '''chronological gap''' between the '''{{ill|Akibayama Kofun Cluster|ja|秋葉山古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}''' and the '''{{ill|Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|ja|長柄桜山古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}'''. Its '''location near the Sagami River''' suggests a '''close connection to marine trade routes''', particularly with the '''Nagara Sakurayama Kofun Group'''. Some scholars believe the tumulus was built by '''the Sōbu Kuni no Miyatsuko (相武国造)''', while others argue that the '''Shinaga Kuni no Miyatsuko (師長国造)''' controlled this region.[https://www.hirahaku.jp/hakubutsukan_archive/kouko/00000035/2.html Hiratsuka City Museum] == Historic Site == === '''Hiratsuka City Designated Cultural Property''' === * '''Important Cultural Property (Tangible Cultural Property)''' ** "Shindo Otsukayama Kofun burial goods" (designation1 February 1, 2010).[http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/bunka/page-c_01316.html Hiratsuka City Cultural Property Database] == References == == External Links == * [http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/zukan/iseki/iseki_03.htm Hiratsuka City Archaeological Records] * '''Double middle-round tumulus''' ({{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=draft|12=draft}}) Since the mound was destroyed before its '''structure could be confirmed''', the exact type will never be known. === === '''Surface Features''' === * '''Stone covering (Fuki-ishi)''' ** A '''1960 excavation''' discovered '''fist-sized stones''' at the mound’s summit, suggesting a stone covering may have existed. ** However, '''1936 excavation records make no mention of it''', making this uncertain. * '''Stepped construction (Dan-chiku)''' ** No evidence was found. * '''Haniwa (ceramic tomb markers)''' ** None were discovered. * '''Moat (Shuchu-kyokusen)''' ** No moat was found. The '''burial chambers''' were located '''0.75–0.8 meters underground''' for the '''clay chamber burial''', and '''1.3 meters underground''' for the '''wooden coffin burial'''. == burial goods == [[File:真土大塚山古墳出土 三角縁四神二獣鏡 (J-23148).JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Sankakuen Shijin Nijukyo mirror}}{{small|On display at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館|12=draft|12=draft}}.}}]] burial goods from '''both burials''' include: === === '''Wooden Coffin Burial''' === Discovered '''before World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館|12=draft|12=draft}}''': * '''1 {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡|1=Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|12=draft|12=draft}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror)''' ** '''Identical to a mirror''' found in the '''{{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}''' (Kyoto), indicating a connection to '''the Yamato region'''. * '''Multiple {{ill|Kudatama|ja|管玉|12=draft|12=draft}} (tube beads) and circular bronze ornaments''' * '''39 bronze arrowheads''' * '''2 iron axes''' * '''1 sword fragment''' * '''1 knife fragment''' * '''Pottery fragments''' ** Believed to date from the '''late Yayoi period''' to the '''early Kofun period'''. === === '''Clay Chamber Burial''' === Excavated '''after World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Hiratsuka City Museum|ja|平塚市博物館|12=draft|12=draft}}''': * '''1 Four Beast Mirror (変形四獣鏡)''' * '''1 Crystal Magatama bead''' * '''2 Crystal "abacus" beads''' * '''150 glass beads''' * '''1 bronze arrowhead''' * '''3 bronze bells''' * '''1 spear-plane (槍鉋, yari-ganna)''' * '''Pottery fragments''' ** Dated to the '''late Yayoi period''' or '''early Kofun period'''. File:真土大塚山古墳出土 銅鏃.JPG|Bronze arrowheads
{{small|On display at the Matsudo City Museum.}} == Historical Significance == Although the mound itself '''was lost''', burial goods confirm that the person buried here had '''strong ties to the Yamato court'''. The kofun was likely built between the '''late 3rd century and mid-4th century''', or possibly in the '''late 4th century'''. It fills a '''chronological gap''' between the '''{{ill|Akibayama Kofun Cluster|ja|秋葉山古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}''' and the '''{{ill|Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|ja|長柄桜山古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}'''. Its '''location near the Sagami River''' suggests a '''close connection to marine trade routes''', particularly with the '''Nagara Sakurayama Kofun Group'''. Some scholars believe the tumulus was built by '''the Sōbu Kuni no Miyatsuko (相武国造)''', while others argue that the '''Shinaga Kuni no Miyatsuko (師長国造)''' controlled this region.[https://www.hirahaku.jp/hakubutsukan_archive/kouko/00000035/2.html Hiratsuka City Museum] == Historic Site == === '''Hiratsuka City Designated Cultural Property''' === * '''Important Cultural Property (Tangible Cultural Property)''' ** "Shindo Otsukayama Kofun burial goods" (designation1 February 1, 2010).[http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/bunka/page-c_01316.html Hiratsuka City Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Shindo Otsukayama Kofun | native_name = 真土大塚山古墳 | location = {{ill|Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|ja|平塚市|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県|12=draft|12=draft}}, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|35|21|31.4|N|139|20|54.8|E|display=inline,title}} | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=draft|12=draft}} / {{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}} / {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft|12=draft}} | length = Unknown | built = Late 3rd century - Mid 4th century (or late 4th century) | burial = Wooden coffin burial, {{ill|Nendo-kaku|ja|粘土槨|1=Clay coffin chamber|1=Clay coffin chamber|12=draft|12=draft}} (clay chamber) | burial goods = {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡|1=Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|12=draft|12=draft}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror), weapons, jewelry | designation1 = None | map = Japan Kanagawa | map_caption = location in Kanagawa Prefecture | image = [[File:Shindo Otsukayama Kofun, funkyu.jpg|280px]]
Reconstructed mound in Shindo Otsukayama Park }} '''{{ill|Shindo Otsukayama Kofun|ja|真土大塚山古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}''' was an ancient Kofun located in '''{{ill|Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|ja|平塚市|12=draft|12=draft}}, Japan'''. The site is '''now lost''', but burial goods from the burial have been designation1 as an '''Important Cultural Property of Hiratsuka City'''. The original type of the tumulus is debated, with '''three competing theories''': 1. '''{{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=draft|12=draft}} (double middle-round tumulus)''' 2. '''{{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}} (keyhole-shaped tumulus)''' 3. '''{{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft|12=draft}} (rectangular-front tumulus)''' However, '''no excavation was conducted before the mound was destroyed''', making its true form uncertain. == Discovery and Excavation == On '''March 18, 1935''', a '''local resident''' discovered a '''mirror, bronze arrowheads, a bronze bell, and iron swords''' while digging up tree roots. A '''field survey''' was conducted on '''March 20''', followed by a full '''excavation and mapping of the tumulus in January 1936'''. In '''1960''', another '''excavation and mapping''' took place, leading to new interpretations of the kofun's type. In '''2016''', a '''re-evaluation''' suggested that it may have been a '''{{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=draft|12=draft}}'''. Today, a '''reconstructed mound''' is preserved '''inside Shindo Otsukayama Park'''. == location == Shindo Otsukayama Kofun was built on a '''sand dune ridge''' along '''{{ill|Sagami Bay|ja|相模湾|12=draft|12=draft}}'''. At the time of excavation, the tumulus sat '''19.5 meters above sea level''', '''11 meters higher than nearby rice fields''', making it the '''highest point in the surrounding lowland'''. Because it was '''built on sand dunes''', early researchers '''nicknamed it "the sand dune tumulus"'''. The surrounding land was '''not highly fertile''', and no large settlements were found nearby. However, the kofun’s '''strategic location''' near both '''Sagami Bay''' and the '''Sagami River mouth''' suggests that it was constructed as a '''major landmark on a transportation route'''. == Structure == The mound was '''never fully excavated''', and its '''exact type remains unknown'''. Based on surveys, three different hypotheses have been proposed: 1. '''Keyhole-shaped tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}}) 2. '''Rectangular-front tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft|12=draft}}) 3. '''Double middle-round tumulus''' ({{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=draft|12=draft}}) Since the mound was destroyed before its '''structure could be confirmed''', the exact type will never be known. === === '''Surface Features''' === * '''Stone covering (Fuki-ishi)''' ** A '''1960 excavation''' discovered '''fist-sized stones''' at the mound’s summit, suggesting a stone covering may have existed. ** However, '''1936 excavation records make no mention of it''', making this uncertain. * '''Stepped construction (Dan-chiku)''' ** No evidence was found. * '''Haniwa (ceramic tomb markers)''' ** None were discovered. * '''Moat (Shuchu-kyokusen)''' ** No moat was found. The '''burial chambers''' were located '''0.75–0.8 meters underground''' for the '''clay chamber burial''', and '''1.3 meters underground''' for the '''wooden coffin burial'''. == burial goods == [[File:真土大塚山古墳出土 三角縁四神二獣鏡 (J-23148).JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Sankakuen Shijin Nijukyo mirror}}{{small|On display at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館|12=draft|12=draft}}.}}]] burial goods from '''both burials''' include: === === '''Wooden Coffin Burial''' === Discovered '''before World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館|12=draft|12=draft}}''': * '''1 {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡|1=Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|12=draft|12=draft}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror)''' ** '''Identical to a mirror''' found in the '''{{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}''' (Kyoto), indicating a connection to '''the Yamato region'''. * '''Multiple {{ill|Kudatama|ja|管玉|12=draft|12=draft}} (tube beads) and circular bronze ornaments''' * '''39 bronze arrowheads''' * '''2 iron axes''' * '''1 sword fragment''' * '''1 knife fragment''' * '''Pottery fragments''' ** Believed to date from the '''late Yayoi period''' to the '''early Kofun period'''. === === '''Clay Chamber Burial''' === Excavated '''after World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Hiratsuka City Museum|ja|平塚市博物館|12=draft|12=draft}}''': * '''1 Four Beast Mirror (変形四獣鏡)''' * '''1 Crystal Magatama bead''' * '''2 Crystal "abacus" beads''' * '''150 glass beads''' * '''1 bronze arrowhead''' * '''3 bronze bells''' * '''1 spear-plane (槍鉋, yari-ganna)''' * '''Pottery fragments''' ** Dated to the '''late Yayoi period''' or '''early Kofun period'''. {{small|On display at the Matsudo City Museum.}} == Historical Significance == Although the mound itself '''was lost''', burial goods confirm that the person buried here had '''strong ties to the Yamato court'''. The kofun was likely built between the '''late 3rd century and mid-4th century''', or possibly in the '''late 4th century'''. It fills a '''chronological gap''' between the '''{{ill|Akibayama Kofun Cluster|ja|秋葉山古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}''' and the '''{{ill|Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|ja|長柄桜山古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}'''. Its '''location near the Sagami River''' suggests a '''close connection to marine trade routes''', particularly with the '''Nagara Sakurayama Kofun Group'''. Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Shindo Otsukayama Kofun | native_name = 真土大塚山古墳 | location = {{ill|Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|ja|平塚市|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県|12=draft|12=draft}}, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|35|21|31.4|N|139|20|54.8|E|display=inline,title}} | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=draft|12=draft}} / {{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}} / {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft|12=draft}} | length = Unknown | built = Late 3rd century - Mid 4th century (or late 4th century) | burial = Wooden coffin burial, {{ill|Nendo-kaku|ja|粘土槨|1=Clay coffin chamber|1=Clay coffin chamber|12=draft|12=draft}} (clay chamber) | burial goods = {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡|1=Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|12=draft|12=draft}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror), weapons, jewelry | designation1 = None | map = Japan Kanagawa | map_caption = location in Kanagawa Prefecture | image = [[File:Shindo Otsukayama Kofun, funkyu.jpg|280px]]
Reconstructed mound in Shindo Otsukayama Park }} '''{{ill|Shindo Otsukayama Kofun|ja|真土大塚山古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}''' was an ancient Kofun located in '''{{ill|Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|ja|平塚市|12=draft|12=draft}}, Japan'''. The site is '''now lost''', but burial goods from the burial have been designation1 as an '''Important Cultural Property of Hiratsuka City'''. The original type of the tumulus is debated, with '''three competing theories''': 1. '''{{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=draft|12=draft}} (double middle-round tumulus)''' 2. '''{{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}} (keyhole-shaped tumulus)''' 3. '''{{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft|12=draft}} (rectangular-front tumulus)''' However, '''no excavation was conducted before the mound was destroyed''', making its true form uncertain. == Discovery and Excavation == On '''March 18, 1935''', a '''local resident''' discovered a '''mirror, bronze arrowheads, a bronze bell, and iron swords''' while digging up tree roots. A '''field survey''' was conducted on '''March 20''', followed by a full '''excavation and mapping of the tumulus in January 1936'''. In '''1960''', another '''excavation and mapping''' took place, leading to new interpretations of the kofun's type. In '''2016''', a '''re-evaluation''' suggested that it may have been a '''{{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=draft|12=draft}}'''. Today, a '''reconstructed mound''' is preserved '''inside Shindo Otsukayama Park'''. == location == Shindo Otsukayama Kofun was built on a '''sand dune ridge''' along '''{{ill|Sagami Bay|ja|相模湾|12=draft|12=draft}}'''. At the time of excavation, the tumulus sat '''19.5 meters above sea level''', '''11 meters higher than nearby rice fields''', making it the '''highest point in the surrounding lowland'''. Because it was '''built on sand dunes''', early researchers '''nicknamed it "the sand dune tumulus"'''. The surrounding land was '''not highly fertile''', and no large settlements were found nearby. However, the kofun’s '''strategic location''' near both '''Sagami Bay''' and the '''Sagami River mouth''' suggests that it was constructed as a '''major landmark on a transportation route'''. == Structure == The mound was '''never fully excavated''', and its '''exact type remains unknown'''. Based on surveys, three different hypotheses have been proposed: 1. '''Keyhole-shaped tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}}) 2. '''Rectangular-front tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft|12=draft}}) 3. '''Double middle-round tumulus''' ({{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=draft|12=draft}}) Since the mound was destroyed before its '''structure could be confirmed''', the exact type will never be known. === === '''Surface Features''' === * '''Stone covering (Fuki-ishi)''' ** A '''1960 excavation''' discovered '''fist-sized stones''' at the mound’s summit, suggesting a stone covering may have existed. ** However, '''1936 excavation records make no mention of it''', making this uncertain. * '''Stepped construction (Dan-chiku)''' ** No evidence was found. * '''Haniwa (ceramic tomb markers)''' ** None were discovered. * '''Moat (Shuchu-kyokusen)''' ** No moat was found. The '''burial chambers''' were located '''0.75–0.8 meters underground''' for the '''clay chamber burial''', and '''1.3 meters underground''' for the '''wooden coffin burial'''. == burial goods == [[File:真土大塚山古墳出土 三角縁四神二獣鏡 (J-23148).JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Sankakuen Shijin Nijukyo mirror}}{{small|On display at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館|12=draft|12=draft}}.}}]] burial goods from '''both burials''' include: === === '''Wooden Coffin Burial''' === Discovered '''before World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館|12=draft|12=draft}}''': * '''1 {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡|1=Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|12=draft|12=draft}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror)''' ** '''Identical to a mirror''' found in the '''{{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}''' (Kyoto), indicating a connection to '''the Yamato region'''. * '''Multiple {{ill|Kudatama|ja|管玉|12=draft|12=draft}} (tube beads) and circular bronze ornaments''' * '''39 bronze arrowheads''' * '''2 iron axes''' * '''1 sword fragment''' * '''1 knife fragment''' * '''Pottery fragments''' ** Believed to date from the '''late Yayoi period''' to the '''early Kofun period'''. === === '''Clay Chamber Burial''' === Excavated '''after World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Hiratsuka City Museum|ja|平塚市博物館|12=draft|12=draft}}''': * '''1 Four Beast Mirror (変形四獣鏡)''' * '''1 Crystal Magatama bead''' * '''2 Crystal "abacus" beads''' * '''150 glass beads''' * '''1 bronze arrowhead''' * '''3 bronze bells''' * '''1 spear-plane (槍鉋, yari-ganna)''' * '''Pottery fragments''' ** Dated to the '''late Yayoi period''' or '''early Kofun period'''. File:真土大塚山古墳出土 銅鏃.JPG|Bronze arrowheads
{{small|On display at the Matsudo City Museum.}} == Historical Significance == Although the mound itself '''was lost''', burial goods confirm that the person buried here had '''strong ties to the Yamato court'''. The kofun was likely built between the '''late 3rd century and mid-4th century''', or possibly in the '''late 4th century'''. It fills a '''chronological gap''' between the '''{{ill|Akibayama Kofun Cluster|ja|秋葉山古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}''' and the '''{{ill|Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|ja|長柄桜山古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}'''. Its '''location near the Sagami River''' suggests a '''close connection to marine trade routes''', particularly with the '''Nagara Sakurayama Kofun Group'''. Some scholars believe the tumulus was built by '''the Sōbu Kuni no Miyatsuko (相武国造)''', while others argue that the '''Shinaga Kuni no Miyatsuko (師長国造)''' controlled this region.[https://www.hirahaku.jp/hakubutsukan_archive/kouko/00000035/2.html Hiratsuka City Museum] == Historic Site == === '''Hiratsuka City Designated Cultural Property''' === * '''Important Cultural Property (Tangible Cultural Property)''' ** "Shindo Otsukayama Kofun burial goods" (designation1 February 1, 2010).[http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/bunka/page-c_01316.html Hiratsuka City Cultural Property Database] == References == == External Links == * [http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/zukan/iseki/iseki_03.htm Hiratsuka City Archaeological Records] * Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Shindo Otsukayama Kofun | native_name = 真土大塚山古墳 | location = {{ill|Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|ja|平塚市|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県|12=draft|12=draft}}, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|35|21|31.4|N|139|20|54.8|E|display=inline,title}} | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=draft|12=draft}} / {{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}} / {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft|12=draft}} | length = Unknown | built = Late 3rd century - Mid 4th century (or late 4th century) | burial = Wooden coffin burial, {{ill|Nendo-kaku|ja|粘土槨|1=Clay coffin chamber|1=Clay coffin chamber|12=draft|12=draft}} (clay chamber) | burial goods = {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡|1=Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|12=draft|12=draft}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror), weapons, jewelry | designation1 = None | map = Japan Kanagawa | map_caption = location in Kanagawa Prefecture | image = [[File:Shindo Otsukayama Kofun, funkyu.jpg|280px]]
Reconstructed mound in Shindo Otsukayama Park }} '''{{ill|Shindo Otsukayama Kofun|ja|真土大塚山古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}''' was an ancient Kofun located in '''{{ill|Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|ja|平塚市|12=draft|12=draft}}, Japan'''. The site is '''now lost''', but burial goods from the burial have been designation1 as an '''Important Cultural Property of Hiratsuka City'''. The original type of the tumulus is debated, with '''three competing theories''': 1. '''{{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=draft|12=draft}} (double middle-round tumulus)''' 2. '''{{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}} (keyhole-shaped tumulus)''' 3. '''{{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft|12=draft}} (rectangular-front tumulus)''' However, '''no excavation was conducted before the mound was destroyed''', making its true form uncertain. == Discovery and Excavation == On '''March 18, 1935''', a '''local resident''' discovered a '''mirror, bronze arrowheads, a bronze bell, and iron swords''' while digging up tree roots. A '''field survey''' was conducted on '''March 20''', followed by a full '''excavation and mapping of the tumulus in January 1936'''. In '''1960''', another '''excavation and mapping''' took place, leading to new interpretations of the kofun's type. In '''2016''', a '''re-evaluation''' suggested that it may have been a '''{{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=draft|12=draft}}'''. Today, a '''reconstructed mound''' is preserved '''inside Shindo Otsukayama Park'''. == location == Shindo Otsukayama Kofun was built on a '''sand dune ridge''' along '''{{ill|Sagami Bay|ja|相模湾|12=draft|12=draft}}'''. At the time of excavation, the tumulus sat '''19.5 meters above sea level''', '''11 meters higher than nearby rice fields''', making it the '''highest point in the surrounding lowland'''. Because it was '''built on sand dunes''', early researchers '''nicknamed it "the sand dune tumulus"'''. The surrounding land was '''not highly fertile''', and no large settlements were found nearby. However, the kofun’s '''strategic location''' near both '''Sagami Bay''' and the '''Sagami River mouth''' suggests that it was constructed as a '''major landmark on a transportation route'''. == Structure == The mound was '''never fully excavated''', and its '''exact type remains unknown'''. Based on surveys, three different hypotheses have been proposed: 1. '''Keyhole-shaped tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}}) 2. '''Rectangular-front tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft|12=draft}}) 3. '''Double middle-round tumulus''' ({{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=draft|12=draft}}) Since the mound was destroyed before its '''structure could be confirmed''', the exact type will never be known. === === '''Surface Features''' === * '''Stone covering (Fuki-ishi)''' ** A '''1960 excavation''' discovered '''fist-sized stones''' at the mound’s summit, suggesting a stone covering may have existed. ** However, '''1936 excavation records make no mention of it''', making this uncertain. * '''Stepped construction (Dan-chiku)''' ** No evidence was found. * '''Haniwa (ceramic tomb markers)''' ** None were discovered. * '''Moat (Shuchu-kyokusen)''' ** No moat was found. The '''burial chambers''' were located '''0.75–0.8 meters underground''' for the '''clay chamber burial''', and '''1.3 meters underground''' for the '''wooden coffin burial'''. == burial goods == [[File:真土大塚山古墳出土 三角縁四神二獣鏡 (J-23148).JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Sankakuen Shijin Nijukyo mirror}}{{small|On display at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館|12=draft|12=draft}}.}}]] burial goods from '''both burials''' include: === === '''Wooden Coffin Burial''' === Discovered '''before World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館|12=draft|12=draft}}''': * '''1 {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡|1=Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|12=draft|12=draft}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror)''' ** '''Identical to a mirror''' found in the '''{{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}''' (Kyoto), indicating a connection to '''the Yamato region'''. * '''Multiple {{ill|Kudatama|ja|管玉|12=draft|12=draft}} (tube beads) and circular bronze ornaments''' * '''39 bronze arrowheads''' * '''2 iron axes''' * '''1 sword fragment''' * '''1 knife fragment''' * '''Pottery fragments''' ** Believed to date from the '''late Yayoi period''' to the '''early Kofun period'''. === === '''Clay Chamber Burial''' === Excavated '''after World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Hiratsuka City Museum|ja|平塚市博物館|12=draft|12=draft}}''': * '''1 Four Beast Mirror (変形四獣鏡)''' * '''1 Crystal Magatama bead''' * '''2 Crystal "abacus" beads''' * '''150 glass beads''' * '''1 bronze arrowhead''' * '''3 bronze bells''' * '''1 spear-plane (槍鉋, yari-ganna)''' * '''Pottery fragments''' ** Dated to the '''late Yayoi period''' or '''early Kofun period'''. File:真土大塚山古墳出土 銅鏃.JPG|Bronze arrowheads
{{small|On display at the Matsudo City Museum.}} == Historical Significance == Although the mound itself '''was lost''', burial goods confirm that the person buried here had '''strong ties to the Yamato court'''. The kofun was likely built between the '''late 3rd century and mid-4th century''', or possibly in the '''late 4th century'''. It fills a '''chronological gap''' between the '''{{ill|Akibayama Kofun Cluster|ja|秋葉山古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}''' and the '''{{ill|Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|ja|長柄桜山古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}'''. Its '''location near the Sagami River''' suggests a '''close connection to marine trade routes''', particularly with the '''Nagara Sakurayama Kofun Group'''. Some scholars believe the tumulus was built by '''the Sōbu Kuni no Miyatsuko (相武国造)''', while others argue that the '''Shinaga Kuni no Miyatsuko (師長国造)''' controlled this region.[https://www.hirahaku.jp/hakubutsukan_archive/kouko/00000035/2.html Hiratsuka City Museum] == Historic Site == === '''Hiratsuka City Designated Cultural Property''' === * '''Important Cultural Property (Tangible Cultural Property)''' ** "Shindo Otsukayama Kofun burial goods" (designation1 February 1, 2010).[http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/bunka/page-c_01316.html Hiratsuka City Cultural Property Database] == References == == External Links == * [http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/zukan/iseki/iseki_03.htm Hiratsuka City Archaeological Records] * '''{{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft|12=draft}} (rectangular-front tumulus)''' However, '''no excavation was conducted before the mound was destroyed''', making its true form uncertain. == Discovery and Excavation == On '''March 18, 1935''', a '''local resident''' discovered a '''mirror, bronze arrowheads, a bronze bell, and iron swords''' while digging up tree roots. A '''field survey''' was conducted on '''March 20''', followed by a full '''excavation and mapping of the tumulus in January 1936'''. In '''1960''', another '''excavation and mapping''' took place, leading to new interpretations of the kofun's type. In '''2016''', a '''re-evaluation''' suggested that it may have been a '''{{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=draft|12=draft}}'''. Today, a '''reconstructed mound''' is preserved '''inside Shindo Otsukayama Park'''. == location == Shindo Otsukayama Kofun was built on a '''sand dune ridge''' along '''{{ill|Sagami Bay|ja|相模湾|12=draft|12=draft}}'''. At the time of excavation, the tumulus sat '''19.5 meters above sea level''', '''11 meters higher than nearby rice fields''', making it the '''highest point in the surrounding lowland'''. Because it was '''built on sand dunes''', early researchers '''nicknamed it "the sand dune tumulus"'''. The surrounding land was '''not highly fertile''', and no large settlements were found nearby. However, the kofun’s '''strategic location''' near both '''Sagami Bay''' and the '''Sagami River mouth''' suggests that it was constructed as a '''major landmark on a transportation route'''. == Structure == The mound was '''never fully excavated''', and its '''exact type remains unknown'''. Based on surveys, three different hypotheses have been proposed: 1. '''Keyhole-shaped tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}}) 2. '''Rectangular-front tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=draft|12=draft}}) 3. '''Double middle-round tumulus''' ({{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=draft|12=draft}}) Since the mound was destroyed before its '''structure could be confirmed''', the exact type will never be known. === === '''Surface Features''' === * '''Stone covering (Fuki-ishi)''' ** A '''1960 excavation''' discovered '''fist-sized stones''' at the mound’s summit, suggesting a stone covering may have existed. ** However, '''1936 excavation records make no mention of it''', making this uncertain. * '''Stepped construction (Dan-chiku)''' ** No evidence was found. * '''Haniwa (ceramic tomb markers)''' ** None were discovered. * '''Moat (Shuchu-kyokusen)''' ** No moat was found. The '''burial chambers''' were located '''0.75–0.8 meters underground''' for the '''clay chamber burial''', and '''1.3 meters underground''' for the '''wooden coffin burial'''. == burial goods == [[File:真土大塚山古墳出土 三角縁四神二獣鏡 (J-23148).JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Sankakuen Shijin Nijukyo mirror}}{{small|On display at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館|12=draft|12=draft}}.}}]] burial goods from '''both burials''' include: === === '''Wooden Coffin Burial''' === Discovered '''before World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館|12=draft|12=draft}}''': * '''1 {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡|1=Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|12=draft|12=draft}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror)''' ** '''Identical to a mirror''' found in the '''{{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}''' (Kyoto), indicating a connection to '''the Yamato region'''. * '''Multiple {{ill|Kudatama|ja|管玉|12=draft|12=draft}} (tube beads) and circular bronze ornaments''' * '''39 bronze arrowheads''' * '''2 iron axes''' * '''1 sword fragment''' * '''1 knife fragment''' * '''Pottery fragments''' ** Believed to date from the '''late Yayoi period''' to the '''early Kofun period'''. === === '''Clay Chamber Burial''' === Excavated '''after World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Hiratsuka City Museum|ja|平塚市博物館|12=draft|12=draft}}''': * '''1 Four Beast Mirror (変形四獣鏡)''' * '''1 Crystal Magatama bead''' * '''2 Crystal "abacus" beads''' * '''150 glass beads''' * '''1 bronze arrowhead''' * '''3 bronze bells''' * '''1 spear-plane (槍鉋, yari-ganna)''' * '''Pottery fragments''' ** Dated to the '''late Yayoi period''' or '''early Kofun period'''. {{small|On display at the Matsudo City Museum.}} == Historical Significance == Although the mound itself '''was lost''', burial goods confirm that the person buried here had '''strong ties to the Yamato court'''. The kofun was likely built between the '''late 3rd century and mid-4th century''', or possibly in the '''late 4th century'''. It fills a '''chronological gap''' between the '''{{ill|Akibayama Kofun Cluster|ja|秋葉山古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}''' and the '''{{ill|Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|ja|長柄桜山古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}'''. Its '''location near the Sagami River''' suggests a '''close connection to marine trade routes''', particularly with the '''Nagara Sakurayama Kofun Group'''. Some scholars believe the tumulus was built by '''the Sōbu Kuni no Miyatsuko (相武国造)''', while others argue that the '''Shinaga Kuni no Miyatsuko (師長国造)''' controlled this region.[https://www.hirahaku.jp/hakubutsukan_archive/kouko/00000035/2.html Hiratsuka City Museum] == Historic Site == === '''Hiratsuka City Designated Cultural Property''' === * '''Important Cultural Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox Kofun | name = Shindo Otsukayama Kofun | native_name = 真土大塚山古墳 | location = {{ill|Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|ja|平塚市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|35|21|31.4|N|139|20|54.8|E|display=inline,title}} | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} / {{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} / {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} | length = Unknown | built = Late 3rd century - Mid 4th century (or late 4th century) | burial = Wooden coffin burial, {{ill|Nendo-kaku|ja|粘土槨|1=Clay coffin chamber|1=Clay coffin chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (clay chamber) | burial goods = {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡|1=Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror), weapons, jewelry | designation1 = None | map = Japan Kanagawa | map_caption = location in Kanagawa Prefecture | image = [[File:Shindo Otsukayama Kofun, funkyu.jpg|280px]]
Reconstructed mound in Shindo Otsukayama Park }} '''{{ill|Shindo Otsukayama Kofun|ja|真土大塚山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' was an ancient Kofun located in '''{{ill|Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|ja|平塚市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Japan'''. The site is '''now lost''', but burial goods from the burial have been designation1 as an '''Important Cultural Property of Hiratsuka City'''. The original type of the tumulus is debated, with '''three competing theories''': 1. '''{{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (double middle-round tumulus)''' 2. '''{{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (keyhole-shaped tumulus)''' 3. '''{{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (rectangular-front tumulus)''' However, '''no excavation was conducted before the mound was destroyed''', making its true form uncertain. == Discovery and Excavation == On '''March 18, 1935''', a '''local resident''' discovered a '''mirror, bronze arrowheads, a bronze bell, and iron swords''' while digging up tree roots. A '''field survey''' was conducted on '''March 20''', followed by a full '''excavation and mapping of the tumulus in January 1936'''. In '''1960''', another '''excavation and mapping''' took place, leading to new interpretations of the kofun's type. In '''2016''', a '''re-evaluation''' suggested that it may have been a '''{{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'''. Today, a '''reconstructed mound''' is preserved '''inside Shindo Otsukayama Park'''. == location == Shindo Otsukayama Kofun was built on a '''sand dune ridge''' along '''{{ill|Sagami Bay|ja|相模湾|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'''. At the time of excavation, the tumulus sat '''19.5 meters above sea level''', '''11 meters higher than nearby rice fields''', making it the '''highest point in the surrounding lowland'''. Because it was '''built on sand dunes''', early researchers '''nicknamed it "the sand dune tumulus"'''. The surrounding land was '''not highly fertile''', and no large settlements were found nearby. However, the kofun’s '''strategic location''' near both '''Sagami Bay''' and the '''Sagami River mouth''' suggests that it was constructed as a '''major landmark on a transportation route'''. == Structure == The mound was '''never fully excavated''', and its '''exact type remains unknown'''. Based on surveys, three different hypotheses have been proposed: 1. '''Keyhole-shaped tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) 2. '''Rectangular-front tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) 3. '''Double middle-round tumulus''' ({{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) Since the mound was destroyed before its '''structure could be confirmed''', the exact type will never be known. === === '''Surface Features''' === * '''Stone covering (Fuki-ishi)''' ** A '''1960 excavation''' discovered '''fist-sized stones''' at the mound’s summit, suggesting a stone covering may have existed. ** However, '''1936 excavation records make no mention of it''', making this uncertain. * '''Stepped construction (Dan-chiku)''' ** No evidence was found. * '''Haniwa (ceramic tomb markers)''' ** None were discovered. * '''Moat (Shuchu-kyokusen)''' ** No moat was found. The '''burial chambers''' were located '''0.75–0.8 meters underground''' for the '''clay chamber burial''', and '''1.3 meters underground''' for the '''wooden coffin burial'''. == burial goods == [[File:真土大塚山古墳出土 三角縁四神二獣鏡 (J-23148).JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Sankakuen Shijin Nijukyo mirror}}{{small|On display at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.}}]] burial goods from '''both burials''' include: === === '''Wooden Coffin Burial''' === Discovered '''before World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''': * '''1 {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡|1=Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror)''' ** '''Identical to a mirror''' found in the '''{{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' (Kyoto), indicating a connection to '''the Yamato region'''. * '''Multiple {{ill|Kudatama|ja|管玉|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (tube beads) and circular bronze ornaments''' * '''39 bronze arrowheads''' * '''2 iron axes''' * '''1 sword fragment''' * '''1 knife fragment''' * '''Pottery fragments''' ** Believed to date from the '''late Yayoi period''' to the '''early Kofun period'''. === === '''Clay Chamber Burial''' === Excavated '''after World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Hiratsuka City Museum|ja|平塚市博物館|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''': * '''1 Four Beast Mirror (変形四獣鏡)''' * '''1 Crystal Magatama bead''' * '''2 Crystal "abacus" beads''' * '''150 glass beads''' * '''1 bronze arrowhead''' * '''3 bronze bells''' * '''1 spear-plane (槍鉋, yari-ganna)''' * '''Pottery fragments''' ** Dated to the '''late Yayoi period''' or '''early Kofun period'''. File:真土大塚山古墳出土 銅鏃.JPG|Bronze arrowheads
{{small|On display at the Matsudo City Museum.}} == Historical Significance == Although the mound itself '''was lost''', burial goods confirm that the person buried here had '''strong ties to the Yamato court'''. The kofun was likely built between the '''late 3rd century and mid-4th century''', or possibly in the '''late 4th century'''. It fills a '''chronological gap''' between the '''{{ill|Akibayama Kofun Cluster|ja|秋葉山古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' and the '''{{ill|Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|ja|長柄桜山古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'''. Its '''location near the Sagami River''' suggests a '''close connection to marine trade routes''', particularly with the '''Nagara Sakurayama Kofun Group'''. Some scholars believe the tumulus was built by '''the Sōbu Kuni no Miyatsuko (相武国造)''', while others argue that the '''Shinaga Kuni no Miyatsuko (師長国造)''' controlled this region.[https://www.hirahaku.jp/hakubutsukan_archive/kouko/00000035/2.html Hiratsuka City Museum] == Historic Site == === '''Hiratsuka City Designated Cultural Property''' === * '''Important Cultural Property (Tangible Cultural Property)''' ** "Shindo Otsukayama Kofun burial goods" (designation1 February 1, 2010).[http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/bunka/page-c_01316.html Hiratsuka City Cultural Property Database] == References == == External Links == * [http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/zukan/iseki/iseki_03.htm Hiratsuka City Archaeological Records] * '''Double middle-round tumulus''' ({{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) Since the mound was destroyed before its '''structure could be confirmed''', the exact type will never be known. === === '''Surface Features''' === * '''Stone covering (Fuki-ishi)''' ** A '''1960 excavation''' discovered '''fist-sized stones''' at the mound’s summit, suggesting a stone covering may have existed. ** However, '''1936 excavation records make no mention of it''', making this uncertain. * '''Stepped construction (Dan-chiku)''' ** No evidence was found. * '''Haniwa (ceramic tomb markers)''' ** None were discovered. * '''Moat (Shuchu-kyokusen)''' ** No moat was found. The '''burial chambers''' were located '''0.75–0.8 meters underground''' for the '''clay chamber burial''', and '''1.3 meters underground''' for the '''wooden coffin burial'''. == burial goods == [[File:真土大塚山古墳出土 三角縁四神二獣鏡 (J-23148).JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Sankakuen Shijin Nijukyo mirror}}{{small|On display at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.}}]] burial goods from '''both burials''' include: === === '''Wooden Coffin Burial''' === Discovered '''before World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''': * '''1 {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡|1=Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror)''' ** '''Identical to a mirror''' found in the '''{{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' (Kyoto), indicating a connection to '''the Yamato region'''. * '''Multiple {{ill|Kudatama|ja|管玉|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (tube beads) and circular bronze ornaments''' * '''39 bronze arrowheads''' * '''2 iron axes''' * '''1 sword fragment''' * '''1 knife fragment''' * '''Pottery fragments''' ** Believed to date from the '''late Yayoi period''' to the '''early Kofun period'''. === === '''Clay Chamber Burial''' === Excavated '''after World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Hiratsuka City Museum|ja|平塚市博物館|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''': * '''1 Four Beast Mirror (変形四獣鏡)''' * '''1 Crystal Magatama bead''' * '''2 Crystal "abacus" beads''' * '''150 glass beads''' * '''1 bronze arrowhead''' * '''3 bronze bells''' * '''1 spear-plane (槍鉋, yari-ganna)''' * '''Pottery fragments''' ** Dated to the '''late Yayoi period''' or '''early Kofun period'''. File:真土大塚山古墳出土 銅鏃.JPG|Bronze arrowheads
{{small|On display at the Matsudo City Museum.}} == Historical Significance == Although the mound itself '''was lost''', burial goods confirm that the person buried here had '''strong ties to the Yamato court'''. The kofun was likely built between the '''late 3rd century and mid-4th century''', or possibly in the '''late 4th century'''. It fills a '''chronological gap''' between the '''{{ill|Akibayama Kofun Cluster|ja|秋葉山古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' and the '''{{ill|Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|ja|長柄桜山古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'''. Its '''location near the Sagami River''' suggests a '''close connection to marine trade routes''', particularly with the '''Nagara Sakurayama Kofun Group'''. Some scholars believe the tumulus was built by '''the Sōbu Kuni no Miyatsuko (相武国造)''', while others argue that the '''Shinaga Kuni no Miyatsuko (師長国造)''' controlled this region.[https://www.hirahaku.jp/hakubutsukan_archive/kouko/00000035/2.html Hiratsuka City Museum] == Historic Site == === '''Hiratsuka City Designated Cultural Property''' === * '''Important Cultural Property (Tangible Cultural Property)''' ** "Shindo Otsukayama Kofun burial goods" (designation1 February 1, 2010).[http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/bunka/page-c_01316.html Hiratsuka City Cultural Property Database] == References == == External Links == * [http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/zukan/iseki/iseki_03.htm Hiratsuka City Archaeological Records] * {{日本の古墳 |名称 =真土大塚山古墳 |別名 = |画像 =[[File:Shindo Otsukayama Kofun, funkyu.jpg|280px]] |画像キャプション =再現墳丘（真土大塚山公園内） |所在地 =[[神奈川県]][[平塚市]]真土字十四ノ域 |所属 = |緯度度 =35 |緯度分 =21 |緯度秒 =31.4 |経度度 =139 |経度分 =20 |経度秒 =54.8 |ISO =JP-14 |形状 =[[双方中円墳]]/[[前方後円墳]]/[[前方後方墳]] |築造時期 =[[3世紀]]末-[[4世紀]]中頃（または4世紀後半） |埋葬施設 =[[木棺]]直葬・[[粘土槨]] |規模 =不明 |被葬者 =（一説）[[相武国造]]一族「[https://www.hirahaku.jp/hakubutsukan_archive/kouko/00000035/2.html 真土大塚山古墳]」[[平塚市博物館]] |出土品 =[[三角縁神獣鏡]]ほか副葬品多数 |史跡 =なし |埋蔵文化財包蔵地番号 = |有形文化財 =出土資料（平塚市指定重要文化財） |特記事項 = |アイコン = |ラベル位置 = bottom |地図 = Japan Kanagawa }} '''真土大塚山古墳'''（しんどおおつかやまこふん）は、[[神奈川県]][[平塚市]]真土にあった古墳。出土資料は平塚市指定重要文化財に指定されている。現在では墳丘は失われている。 墳形については[[双方中円墳]]説・[[前方後円墳]]説・[[前方後方墳]]説があるが、墳丘調査が行われないまま消滅したため明らかでない。 ==発見と発掘の経緯== [[1935年]]（昭和10年）[[3月18日]]、地元の住民が松の根を掘っている最中に[[鏡]]、銅鏃、銅鐸、直刀などが出土した。[[3月20日]]には現地調査が行われ、更に翌[[1936年]]（昭和11年）1月に墳丘の測量と[[発掘調査]]が行われた。 [[1960年]]（昭和35年）、改めて墳丘の測量と発掘調査が行われた。[[2016年]]（平成27年）には再調査により、[[双方中円墳]]とする説が浮上した。 現在では、古墳跡の北側の真土大塚山公園内に墳丘が再現されている。 ==立地== 真土大塚山古墳は、[[相模湾]]に沿った砂丘列の上に造られた。海抜19.5メートルの場所にあり、発掘時、周辺にあった水田との標高差は11メートルあったといい、周囲の低地帯の中では一番高い位置にあった。古墳は砂丘の砂地を削り出して整形し、その上に[[盛土]]をしていた。[[砂丘]]の砂地に造られたこともあって、戦前の発掘時には、真土大塚山古墳のことを「砂丘墳」とも呼んだ。 古墳造営当時、古墳周辺は砂丘地であり、生産性は低かったとみられ、周囲からは大きな集落跡も見つかっていないが、相模湾とともに[[相模川]]の河口に近い位置にあり、交通の要衝に造営された古墳であるとみられている。 ==構造== 真土大塚山古墳は2度にわたり発掘調査がおこなわれ、墳丘の測量調査と埋葬施設の調査が行われたが、墳丘に[[トレンチ]]を入れるなどの墳丘本体の調査は実施されなかった。測量調査の結果、双方中円墳説、前方後円墳説の両説が出され、後に調査結果を詳細に再検討した研究者から、前方後方墳説が出されたが、実際の墳丘がどのような形であったのか、調査されることもなく消滅してしまい、今となっては真土大塚山古墳が実際にどのような形をしていたのか、知ることができなくなってしまった。 [[葺石]]については、1960年の発掘時に、墳頂部から握りこぶしの石が見つかったため、存在したとの説もあるが、1936年の調査では全く葺石については言及されていないこともあって確実性に欠ける。[[段築]]については不明で、[[埴輪]]の出土はなく、周濠も存在しない。 埋葬施設は墳丘中央部の地表下75～80センチメートルのところに粘土槨、そして1.3メートル付近には木棺直葬がされていたと見られている。 ==出土品== [[ファイル:真土大塚山古墳出土 三角縁四神二獣鏡 (J-23148).JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|三角縁四神二獣鏡}}{{small|[[東京国立博物館]]展示。}}]] 木棺直葬の主体部から出土品としては戦前の発掘時に[[三角縁神獣鏡]]、管玉・巴形銅器、銅器2、多数の銅鏃39、鉄斧2、[[剣]]の破片1、刀の破片1、[[土器]]の破片であった。[[三角縁神獣鏡]]は[[京都府]]の[[椿井大塚山古墳]]で出土したものと同笵鏡で、土器片は[[弥生時代]]末から[[古墳時代]]初頭にかけてのものとみられている。 [[粘土槨]]から戦後の発掘時には変形四獣鏡1、[[水]]晶製[[勾玉]]1、水晶製算盤玉2、ガラス玉150、銅鏃1、銅鐸3、槍鉋（やりがんな）1、土器片が出土した。やはり土器片は[[弥生時代]]末から[[古墳時代]]初頭のものと見られている。 戦前の出土品はそのほとんどが[[東京国立博物館]]に、戦後の出土品は[[平塚市博物館]]に所蔵されている。 ファイル:真土大塚山古墳出土 銅鏃.JPG|銅鏃
{{small|東京国立博物館蔵、[[松戸市立博物館]]企画展示時に撮影。}} ==特徴== 古墳本体の調査が行われないうちに消滅したため、墳形が不明のままであることなど全容がつかめたとは言いがたいが、三角縁神獣鏡の出土などから、[[畿内]]との強い結びつきがあった人物が葬られた古墳であることは間違いないと見られている。出土品の内容などから、古墳の築造時期は[[3世紀]]末から[[4世紀]]半ば頃、または4世紀後半頃と考えられており、神奈川県内では[[秋葉山古墳群]]と[[長柄桜山古墳群]]をつなぐ時期に造営された可能性が高い。[[相模川]]の河口近くという真土大塚山古墳の立地条件から考えて、海上交通路の近くに造営された長柄桜山古墳群との類似性が特に注目される。 [[相武国造]]に繋がる豪族と見る説もあるが「真土大塚山古墳」平塚市博物館、[[相模川]]より西域は一般に[[師長国造]]の領域とされる。 == 文化財 == === 平塚市指定文化財 === * 重要文化財（有形文化財） ** 変形四獣鏡他 真土大塚山古墳出土資料 一括（考古資料） - 2010年（平成22年）2月1日指定[http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/bunka/page-c_01316.html 変形四獣鏡他 真土大塚山古墳出土資料 一括]（平塚市ホームページ）。。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{Reflist}} == 参考文献 == *「武蔵と相模の古墳」（『季刊考古学』別冊15）[[雄山閣]]、2007年。 * 小市和雄編著 「神奈川県謎解き散歩」、2011年。 == 外部リンク == {{commonscat|Shindo Otsukayama Kofun}} * [http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/zukan/iseki/iseki_03.htm 豪族と古墳 真土大塚山古墳（古墳時代）]　平塚市 * [http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/koen/page-c_02813.html 真土大塚山公園]　平塚市 * [http://www.hirahaku.jp/web_yomimono/kouko/shinoh1.html 真土大塚山古墳]　平塚市博物館 {{Japanese-history-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:しんとおおつかやまこふん}} [[Category:神奈川県の古墳]] [[Category:平塚市の歴史]]

真土大塚山古墳は、[[相模湾]]に沿った砂丘列の上に造られた。海抜19.5メートルの場所にあり、発掘時、周辺にあった水田との標高差は11メートルあったといい、周囲の低地帯の中では一番高い位置にあった。古墳は砂丘の砂地を削り出して整形し、その上に[[盛土]]をしていた。[[砂丘]]の砂地に造られたこともあって、戦前の発掘時には、真土大塚山古墳のことを「砂丘墳」とも呼んだ。 古墳造営当時、古墳周辺は砂丘地であり、生産性は低かったとみられ、周囲からは大きな集落跡も見つかっていないが、相模湾とともに[[相模川]]の河口に近い位置にあり、交通の要衝に造営された古墳であるとみられている。 ==構造== 真土大塚山古墳は2度にわたり発掘調査がおこなわれ、墳丘の測量調査と埋葬施設の調査が行われたが、墳丘に[[トレンチ]]を入れるなどの墳丘本体の調査は実施されなかった。測量調査の結果、双方中円墳説、前方後円墳説の両説が出され、後に調査結果を詳細に再検討した研究者から、前方後方墳説が出されたが、実際の墳丘がどのような形であったのか、調査されることもなく消滅してしまい、今となっては真土大塚山古墳が実際にどのような形をしていたのか、知ることができなくなってしまった。 [[葺石]]については、1960年の発掘時に、墳頂部から握りこぶしの石が見つかったため、存在したとの説もあるが、1936年の調査では全く葺石については言及されていないこともあって確実性に欠ける。[[段築]]については不明で、[[埴輪]]の出土はなく、周濠も存在しない。 埋葬施設は墳丘中央部の地表下75～80センチメートルのところに粘土槨、そして1.3メートル付近には木棺直葬がされていたと見られている。 ==出土品== [[ファイル:真土大塚山古墳出土 三角縁四神二獣鏡 (J-23148).JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|三角縁四神二獣鏡}}{{small|[[東京国立博物館]]展示。}}]] 木棺直葬の主体部から出土品としては戦前の発掘時に[[三角縁神獣鏡]]、管玉・巴形銅器、銅器2、多数の銅鏃39、鉄斧2、[[剣]]の破片1、刀の破片1、[[土器]]の破片であった。[[三角縁神獣鏡]]は[[京都府]]の[[椿井大塚山古墳]]で出土したものと同笵鏡で、土器片は[[弥生時代]]末から[[古墳時代]]初頭にかけてのものとみられている。 [[粘土槨]]から戦後の発掘時には変形四獣鏡1、[[水]]晶製[[勾玉]]1、水晶製算盤玉2、ガラス玉150、銅鏃1、銅鐸3、槍鉋（やりがんな）1、土器片が出土した。やはり土器片は[[弥生時代]]末から[[古墳時代]]初頭のものと見られている。 戦前の出土品はそのほとんどが[[東京国立博物館]]に、戦後の出土品は[[平塚市博物館]]に所蔵されている。 ファイル:真土大塚山古墳出土 銅鏃.JPG|銅鏃
{{small|東京国立博物館蔵、[[松戸市立博物館]]企画展示時に撮影。}} ==特徴== 古墳本体の調査が行われないうちに消滅したため、墳形が不明のままであることなど全容がつかめたとは言いがたいが、三角縁神獣鏡の出土などから、[[畿内]]との強い結びつきがあった人物が葬られた古墳であることは間違いないと見られている。出土品の内容などから、古墳の築造時期は[[3世紀]]末から[[4世紀]]半ば頃、または4世紀後半頃と考えられており、神奈川県内では[[秋葉山古墳群]]と[[長柄桜山古墳群]]をつなぐ時期に造営された可能性が高い。[[相模川]]の河口近くという真土大塚山古墳の立地条件から考えて、海上交通路の近くに造営された長柄桜山古墳群との類似性が特に注目される。 [[相武国造]]に繋がる豪族と見る説もあるが「真土大塚山古墳」平塚市博物館、[[相模川]]より西域は一般に[[師長国造]]の領域とされる。 == 文化財 == === 平塚市指定文化財 === * 重要文化財（有形文化財） ** 変形四獣鏡他 真土大塚山古墳出土資料 一括（考古資料） - 2010年（平成22年）2月1日指定[http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/bunka/page-c_01316.html 変形四獣鏡他 真土大塚山古墳出土資料 一括]（平塚市ホームページ）。。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{Reflist}} == 参考文献 == *「武蔵と相模の古墳」（『季刊考古学』別冊15）[[雄山閣]]、2007年。 * 小市和雄編著 「神奈川県謎解き散歩」、2011年。 == 外部リンク == {{commonscat|Shindo Otsukayama Kofun}} * [http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/zukan/iseki/iseki_03.htm 豪族と古墳 真土大塚山古墳（古墳時代）]　平塚市 * [http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/koen/page-c_02813.html 真土大塚山公園]　平塚市 * [http://www.hirahaku.jp/web_yomimono/kouko/shinoh1.html 真土大塚山古墳]　平塚市博物館 {{Japanese-history-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:しんとおおつかやまこふん}} [[Category:神奈川県の古墳]] [[Category:平塚市の歴史]]

Reconstructed mound in Shindo Otsukayama Park }} '''{{ill|Shindo Otsukayama Kofun|ja|真土大塚山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' was an ancient Kofun located in '''{{ill|Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|ja|平塚市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Japan'''. The site is '''now lost''', but burial goods from the burial have been designation1 as an '''Important Cultural Property of Hiratsuka City'''. The original type of the tumulus is debated, with '''three competing theories''': 1. '''{{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (double middle-round tumulus)''' 2. '''{{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (keyhole-shaped tumulus)''' 3. '''{{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (rectangular-front tumulus)''' However, '''no excavation was conducted before the mound was destroyed''', making its true form uncertain. == Discovery and Excavation == On '''March 18, 1935''', a '''local resident''' discovered a '''mirror, bronze arrowheads, a bronze bell, and iron swords''' while digging up tree roots. A '''field survey''' was conducted on '''March 20''', followed by a full '''excavation and mapping of the tumulus in January 1936'''. In '''1960''', another '''excavation and mapping''' took place, leading to new interpretations of the kofun's type. In '''2016''', a '''re-evaluation''' suggested that it may have been a '''{{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'''. Today, a '''reconstructed mound''' is preserved '''inside Shindo Otsukayama Park'''. == location == Shindo Otsukayama Kofun was built on a '''sand dune ridge''' along '''{{ill|Sagami Bay|ja|相模湾|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'''. At the time of excavation, the tumulus sat '''19.5 meters above sea level''', '''11 meters higher than nearby rice fields''', making it the '''highest point in the surrounding lowland'''. Because it was '''built on sand dunes''', early researchers '''nicknamed it "the sand dune tumulus"'''. The surrounding land was '''not highly fertile''', and no large settlements were found nearby. However, the kofun’s '''strategic location''' near both '''Sagami Bay''' and the '''Sagami River mouth''' suggests that it was constructed as a '''major landmark on a transportation route'''. == Structure == The mound was '''never fully excavated''', and its '''exact type remains unknown'''. Based on surveys, three different hypotheses have been proposed: 1. '''Keyhole-shaped tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) 2. '''Rectangular-front tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) 3. '''Double middle-round tumulus''' ({{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) Since the mound was destroyed before its '''structure could be confirmed''', the exact type will never be known. === === '''Surface Features''' === * '''Stone covering (Fuki-ishi)''' ** A '''1960 excavation''' discovered '''fist-sized stones''' at the mound’s summit, suggesting a stone covering may have existed. ** However, '''1936 excavation records make no mention of it''', making this uncertain. * '''Stepped construction (Dan-chiku)''' ** No evidence was found. * '''Haniwa (ceramic tomb markers)''' ** None were discovered. * '''Moat (Shuchu-kyokusen)''' ** No moat was found. The '''burial chambers''' were located '''0.75–0.8 meters underground''' for the '''clay chamber burial''', and '''1.3 meters underground''' for the '''wooden coffin burial'''. == burial goods == [[File:真土大塚山古墳出土 三角縁四神二獣鏡 (J-23148).JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Sankakuen Shijin Nijukyo mirror}}{{small|On display at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.}}]] burial goods from '''both burials''' include: === === '''Wooden Coffin Burial''' === Discovered '''before World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''': * '''1 {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡|1=Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror)''' ** '''Identical to a mirror''' found in the '''{{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' (Kyoto), indicating a connection to '''the Yamato region'''. * '''Multiple {{ill|Kudatama|ja|管玉|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (tube beads) and circular bronze ornaments''' * '''39 bronze arrowheads''' * '''2 iron axes''' * '''1 sword fragment''' * '''1 knife fragment''' * '''Pottery fragments''' ** Believed to date from the '''late Yayoi period''' to the '''early Kofun period'''. === === '''Clay Chamber Burial''' === Excavated '''after World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Hiratsuka City Museum|ja|平塚市博物館|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''': * '''1 Four Beast Mirror (変形四獣鏡)''' * '''1 Crystal Magatama bead''' * '''2 Crystal "abacus" beads''' * '''150 glass beads''' * '''1 bronze arrowhead''' * '''3 bronze bells''' * '''1 spear-plane (槍鉋, yari-ganna)''' * '''Pottery fragments''' ** Dated to the '''late Yayoi period''' or '''early Kofun period'''. File:真土大塚山古墳出土 銅鏃.JPG|Bronze arrowheads
{{small|On display at the Matsudo City Museum.}} == Historical Significance == Although the mound itself '''was lost''', burial goods confirm that the person buried here had '''strong ties to the Yamato court'''. The kofun was likely built between the '''late 3rd century and mid-4th century''', or possibly in the '''late 4th century'''. It fills a '''chronological gap''' between the '''{{ill|Akibayama Kofun Cluster|ja|秋葉山古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' and the '''{{ill|Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|ja|長柄桜山古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'''. Its '''location near the Sagami River''' suggests a '''close connection to marine trade routes''', particularly with the '''Nagara Sakurayama Kofun Group'''. Some scholars believe the tumulus was built by '''the Sōbu Kuni no Miyatsuko (相武国造)''', while others argue that the '''Shinaga Kuni no Miyatsuko (師長国造)''' controlled this region.[https://www.hirahaku.jp/hakubutsukan_archive/kouko/00000035/2.html Hiratsuka City Museum] == Historic Site == === '''Hiratsuka City Designated Cultural Property''' === * '''Important Cultural Property (Tangible Cultural Property)''' ** "Shindo Otsukayama Kofun burial goods" (designation1 February 1, 2010).[http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/bunka/page-c_01316.html Hiratsuka City Reconstructed mound in Shindo Otsukayama Park }} '''{{ill|Shindo Otsukayama Kofun|ja|真土大塚山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' was an ancient Kofun located in '''{{ill|Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|ja|平塚市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Japan'''. The site is '''now lost''', but burial goods from the burial have been designation1 as an '''Important Cultural Property of Hiratsuka City'''. The original type of the tumulus is debated, with '''three competing theories''': 1. '''{{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (double middle-round tumulus)''' 2. '''{{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (keyhole-shaped tumulus)''' 3. '''{{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (rectangular-front tumulus)''' However, '''no excavation was conducted before the mound was destroyed''', making its true form uncertain. == Discovery and Excavation == On '''March 18, 1935''', a '''local resident''' discovered a '''mirror, bronze arrowheads, a bronze bell, and iron swords''' while digging up tree roots. A '''field survey''' was conducted on '''March 20''', followed by a full '''excavation and mapping of the tumulus in January 1936'''. In '''1960''', another '''excavation and mapping''' took place, leading to new interpretations of the kofun's type. In '''2016''', a '''re-evaluation''' suggested that it may have been a '''{{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'''. Today, a '''reconstructed mound''' is preserved '''inside Shindo Otsukayama Park'''. == location == Shindo Otsukayama Kofun was built on a '''sand dune ridge''' along '''{{ill|Sagami Bay|ja|相模湾|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'''. At the time of excavation, the tumulus sat '''19.5 meters above sea level''', '''11 meters higher than nearby rice fields''', making it the '''highest point in the surrounding lowland'''. Because it was '''built on sand dunes''', early researchers '''nicknamed it "the sand dune tumulus"'''. The surrounding land was '''not highly fertile''', and no large settlements were found nearby. However, the kofun’s '''strategic location''' near both '''Sagami Bay''' and the '''Sagami River mouth''' suggests that it was constructed as a '''major landmark on a transportation route'''. == Structure == The mound was '''never fully excavated''', and its '''exact type remains unknown'''. Based on surveys, three different hypotheses have been proposed: 1. '''Keyhole-shaped tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) 2. '''Rectangular-front tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) 3. '''Double middle-round tumulus''' ({{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) Since the mound was destroyed before its '''structure could be confirmed''', the exact type will never be known. === === '''Surface Features''' === * '''Stone covering (Fuki-ishi)''' ** A '''1960 excavation''' discovered '''fist-sized stones''' at the mound’s summit, suggesting a stone covering may have existed. ** However, '''1936 excavation records make no mention of it''', making this uncertain. * '''Stepped construction (Dan-chiku)''' ** No evidence was found. * '''Haniwa (ceramic tomb markers)''' ** None were discovered. * '''Moat (Shuchu-kyokusen)''' ** No moat was found. The '''burial chambers''' were located '''0.75–0.8 meters underground''' for the '''clay chamber burial''', and '''1.3 meters underground''' for the '''wooden coffin burial'''. == burial goods == [[File:真土大塚山古墳出土 三角縁四神二獣鏡 (J-23148).JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Sankakuen Shijin Nijukyo mirror}}{{small|On display at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.}}]] burial goods from '''both burials''' include: === === '''Wooden Coffin Burial''' === Discovered '''before World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''': * '''1 {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡|1=Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror)''' ** '''Identical to a mirror''' found in the '''{{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' (Kyoto), indicating a connection to '''the Yamato region'''. * '''Multiple {{ill|Kudatama|ja|管玉|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (tube beads) and circular bronze ornaments''' * '''39 bronze arrowheads''' * '''2 iron axes''' * '''1 sword fragment''' * '''1 knife fragment''' * '''Pottery fragments''' ** Believed to date from the '''late Yayoi period''' to the '''early Kofun period'''. === === '''Clay Chamber Burial''' === Excavated '''after World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Hiratsuka City Museum|ja|平塚市博物館|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''': * '''1 Four Beast Mirror (変形四獣鏡)''' * '''1 Crystal Magatama bead''' * '''2 Crystal "abacus" beads''' * '''150 glass beads''' * '''1 bronze arrowhead''' * '''3 bronze bells''' * '''1 spear-plane (槍鉋, yari-ganna)''' * '''Pottery fragments''' ** Dated to the '''late Yayoi period''' or '''early Kofun period'''. File:真土大塚山古墳出土 銅鏃.JPG|Bronze arrowheads
{{small|On display at the Matsudo City Museum.}} == Historical Significance == Although the mound itself '''was lost''', burial goods confirm that the person buried here had '''strong ties to the Yamato court'''. The kofun was likely built between the '''late 3rd century and mid-4th century''', or possibly in the '''late 4th century'''. It fills a '''chronological gap''' between the '''{{ill|Akibayama Kofun Cluster|ja|秋葉山古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' and the '''{{ill|Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|ja|長柄桜山古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'''. Its '''location near the Sagami River''' suggests a '''close connection to marine trade routes''', particularly with the '''Nagara Sakurayama Kofun Group'''. Some scholars believe the tumulus was built by '''the Sōbu Kuni no Miyatsuko (相武国造)''', while others argue that the '''Shinaga Kuni no Miyatsuko (師長国造)''' controlled this region.[https://www.hirahaku.jp/hakubutsukan_archive/kouko/00000035/2.html Hiratsuka City Museum] == Historic Site == === '''Hiratsuka City Designated Cultural Property''' === * '''Important Cultural Property (Tangible Cultural Property)''' ** "Shindo Otsukayama Kofun burial goods" (designation1 February 1, 2010).[http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/bunka/page-c_01316.html Hiratsuka City Cultural Property Database] == References == == External Links == * [http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/zukan/iseki/iseki_03.htm Hiratsuka City Archaeological Records] * Reconstructed mound in Shindo Otsukayama Park }} '''{{ill|Shindo Otsukayama Kofun|ja|真土大塚山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' was an ancient Kofun located in '''{{ill|Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|ja|平塚市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Japan'''. The site is '''now lost''', but burial goods from the burial have been designation1 as an '''Important Cultural Property of Hiratsuka City'''. The original type of the tumulus is debated, with '''three competing theories''': 1. '''{{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (double middle-round tumulus)''' 2. '''{{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (keyhole-shaped tumulus)''' 3. '''{{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (rectangular-front tumulus)''' However, '''no excavation was conducted before the mound was destroyed''', making its true form uncertain. == Discovery and Excavation == On '''March 18, 1935''', a '''local resident''' discovered a '''mirror, bronze arrowheads, a bronze bell, and iron swords''' while digging up tree roots. A '''field survey''' was conducted on '''March 20''', followed by a full '''excavation and mapping of the tumulus in January 1936'''. In '''1960''', another '''excavation and mapping''' took place, leading to new interpretations of the kofun's type. In '''2016''', a '''re-evaluation''' suggested that it may have been a '''{{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'''. Today, a '''reconstructed mound''' is preserved '''inside Shindo Otsukayama Park'''. == location == Shindo Otsukayama Kofun was built on a '''sand dune ridge''' along '''{{ill|Sagami Bay|ja|相模湾|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'''. At the time of excavation, the tumulus sat '''19.5 meters above sea level''', '''11 meters higher than nearby rice fields''', making it the '''highest point in the surrounding lowland'''. Because it was '''built on sand dunes''', early researchers '''nicknamed it "the sand dune tumulus"'''. The surrounding land was '''not highly fertile''', and no large settlements were found nearby. However, the kofun’s '''strategic location''' near both '''Sagami Bay''' and the '''Sagami River mouth''' suggests that it was constructed as a '''major landmark on a transportation route'''. == Structure == The mound was '''never fully excavated''', and its '''exact type remains unknown'''. Based on surveys, three different hypotheses have been proposed: 1. '''Keyhole-shaped tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) 2. '''Rectangular-front tumulus''' ({{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) 3. '''Double middle-round tumulus''' ({{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) Since the mound was destroyed before its '''structure could be confirmed''', the exact type will never be known. === === '''Surface Features''' === * '''Stone covering (Fuki-ishi)''' ** A '''1960 excavation''' discovered '''fist-sized stones''' at the mound’s summit, suggesting a stone covering may have existed. ** However, '''1936 excavation records make no mention of it''', making this uncertain. * '''Stepped construction (Dan-chiku)''' ** No evidence was found. * '''Haniwa (ceramic tomb markers)''' ** None were discovered. * '''Moat (Shuchu-kyokusen)''' ** No moat was found. The '''burial chambers''' were located '''0.75–0.8 meters underground''' for the '''clay chamber burial''', and '''1.3 meters underground''' for the '''wooden coffin burial'''. == burial goods == [[File:真土大塚山古墳出土 三角縁四神二獣鏡 (J-23148).JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Sankakuen Shijin Nijukyo mirror}}{{small|On display at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.}}]] burial goods from '''both burials''' include: === === '''Wooden Coffin Burial''' === Discovered '''before World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''': * '''1 {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡|1=Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror)''' ** '''Identical to a mirror''' found in the '''{{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' (Kyoto), indicating a connection to '''the Yamato region'''. * '''Multiple {{ill|Kudatama|ja|管玉|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (tube beads) and circular bronze ornaments''' * '''39 bronze arrowheads''' * '''2 iron axes''' * '''1 sword fragment''' * '''1 knife fragment''' * '''Pottery fragments''' ** Believed to date from the '''late Yayoi period''' to the '''early Kofun period'''. === === '''Clay Chamber Burial''' === Excavated '''after World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Hiratsuka City Museum|ja|平塚市博物館|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''': * '''1 Four Beast Mirror (変形四獣鏡)''' * '''1 Crystal Magatama bead''' * '''2 Crystal "abacus" beads''' * '''150 glass beads''' * '''1 bronze arrowhead''' * '''3 bronze bells''' * '''1 spear-plane (槍鉋, yari-ganna)''' * '''Pottery fragments''' ** Dated to the '''late Yayoi period''' or '''early Kofun period'''. File:真土大塚山古墳出土 銅鏃.JPG|Bronze arrowheads
{{small|On display at the Matsudo City Museum.}} == Historical Significance == Although the mound itself '''was lost''', burial goods confirm that the person buried here had '''strong ties to the Yamato court'''. The kofun was likely built between the '''late 3rd century and mid-4th century''', or possibly in the '''late 4th century'''. It fills a '''chronological gap''' between the '''{{ill|Akibayama Kofun Cluster|ja|秋葉山古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' and the '''{{ill|Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|ja|長柄桜山古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'''. Its '''location near the Sagami River''' suggests a '''close connection to marine trade routes''', particularly with the '''Nagara Sakurayama Kofun Group'''. Some scholars believe the tumulus was built by '''the Sōbu Kuni no Miyatsuko (相武国造)''', while others argue that the '''Shinaga Kuni no Miyatsuko (師長国造)''' controlled this region.[https://www.hirahaku.jp/hakubutsukan_archive/kouko/00000035/2.html Hiratsuka City Museum] == Historic Site == === '''Hiratsuka City Designated Cultural Property''' === * '''Important Cultural Property (Tangible Cultural Property)''' ** "Shindo Otsukayama Kofun burial goods" (designation1 February 1, 2010).[http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/bunka/page-c_01316.html Hiratsuka City Cultural Property Database] == References == == External Links == * [http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/zukan/iseki/iseki_03.htm Hiratsuka City Archaeological Records] * '''Double middle-round tumulus''' ({{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) Since the mound was destroyed before its '''structure could be confirmed''', the exact type will never be known. === === '''Surface Features''' === * '''Stone covering (Fuki-ishi)''' ** A '''1960 excavation''' discovered '''fist-sized stones''' at the mound’s summit, suggesting a stone covering may have existed. ** However, '''1936 excavation records make no mention of it''', making this uncertain. * '''Stepped construction (Dan-chiku)''' ** No evidence was found. * '''Haniwa (ceramic tomb markers)''' ** None were discovered. * '''Moat (Shuchu-kyokusen)''' ** No moat was found. The '''burial chambers''' were located '''0.75–0.8 meters underground''' for the '''clay chamber burial''', and '''1.3 meters underground''' for the '''wooden coffin burial'''. == burial goods == [[File:真土大塚山古墳出土 三角縁四神二獣鏡 (J-23148).JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Sankakuen Shijin Nijukyo mirror}}{{small|On display at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.}}]] burial goods from '''both burials''' include: === === '''Wooden Coffin Burial''' === Discovered '''before World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Tokyo National Museum|ja|東京国立博物館|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''': * '''1 {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡|1=Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror)''' ** '''Identical to a mirror''' found in the '''{{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|ja|椿井大塚山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' (Kyoto), indicating a connection to '''the Yamato region'''. * '''Multiple {{ill|Kudatama|ja|管玉|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (tube beads) and circular bronze ornaments''' * '''39 bronze arrowheads''' * '''2 iron axes''' * '''1 sword fragment''' * '''1 knife fragment''' * '''Pottery fragments''' ** Believed to date from the '''late Yayoi period''' to the '''early Kofun period'''. === === '''Clay Chamber Burial''' === Excavated '''after World War II''', these items are housed in the '''{{ill|Hiratsuka City Museum|ja|平塚市博物館|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''': * '''1 Four Beast Mirror (変形四獣鏡)''' * '''1 Crystal Magatama bead''' * '''2 Crystal "abacus" beads''' * '''150 glass beads''' * '''1 bronze arrowhead''' * '''3 bronze bells''' * '''1 spear-plane (槍鉋, yari-ganna)''' * '''Pottery fragments''' ** Dated to the '''late Yayoi period''' or '''early Kofun period'''. File:真土大塚山古墳出土 銅鏃.JPG|Bronze arrowheads
{{small|On display at the Matsudo City Museum.}} == Historical Significance == Although the mound itself '''was lost''', burial goods confirm that the person buried here had '''strong ties to the Yamato court'''. The kofun was likely built between the '''late 3rd century and mid-4th century''', or possibly in the '''late 4th century'''. It fills a '''chronological gap''' between the '''{{ill|Akibayama Kofun Cluster|ja|秋葉山古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''' and the '''{{ill|Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|ja|長柄桜山古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'''. Its '''location near the Sagami River''' suggests a '''close connection to marine trade routes''', particularly with the '''Nagara Sakurayama Kofun Group'''. Some scholars believe the tumulus was built by '''the Sōbu Kuni no Miyatsuko (相武国造)''', while others argue that the '''Shinaga Kuni no Miyatsuko (師長国造)''' controlled this region.[https://www.hirahaku.jp/hakubutsukan_archive/kouko/00000035/2.html Hiratsuka City Museum] == Historic Site == === '''Hiratsuka City Designated Cultural Property''' === * '''Important Cultural Property (Tangible Cultural Property)''' ** "Shindo Otsukayama Kofun burial goods" (designation1 February 1, 2010).[http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/bunka/page-c_01316.html Hiratsuka City
