[[co:commons:Category:Shindo Otsukayama Kofun]][[ja:真土大塚山古墳]] [[co:commons:Category:Shindo Otsukayama Kofun]][[ja:真土大塚山古墳]] [[sn:commons:Category:Shindo Otsukayama Kofun]][[ja:真土大塚山古墳]] {{Infobox ancient site | name = Shindo Otsukayama Kofun | native_name = 真土大塚山古墳 | location = {{ill|Hiratsuka|en|Hiratsuka|WD=Q502199|lt=Hiratsuka, Kanagawa}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|en|Kanagawa Prefecture|WD=Q127513|lt=Kanagawa Prefecture}}, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|35.358722|N|139.348556|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōhō-chūen Kofun|qq=}} / {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun}} / {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoho-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} | length = Unknown | built = Late 3rd century - Mid 4th century (or late 4th century) | burial = Wooden coffin burial, {{ill|Nendo-kaku|ja|粘土槨|1=Clay coffin chamber|1=Clay coffin chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nendo-kaku|13=User:Immanuelle/Clay coffin chamber|qq=}} (clay chamber) | burial goods = {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡|1=Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sankakuen shinjukyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|qq=}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror), weapons, jewelry | designation1 = None | map = Japan Kanagawa | map_caption = location in Kanagawa Prefecture | image = [[File:Shindo Otsukayama Kofun, funkyu.jpg|280px]]
Reconstructed mound in Shindo Otsukayama Park | architectural_styles= {{ill|Q11410445|WD=Q11410445}} }} {{ill|Shindo Otsukayama Kofun|ja|真土大塚山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shindo Otsukayama Kofun}} was an ancient Kofun located in {{ill|Hiratsuka|en|Hiratsuka|WD=Q502199|lt=Hiratsuka, Kanagawa}}, Japan. The site is now lost, but burial goods from the burial have been designation1 as an Important Cultural Property of Hiratsuka City. The original type of the tumulus is debated, with three competing theories: 1. {{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōhō-chūen Kofun}} (double middle-round tumulus) 2. {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun}} (keyhole-shaped tumulus) 3. {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=enwiki is a redirect|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun}} (rectangular-front tumulus) However, no excavation was conducted before the mound was destroyed, making its true form uncertain. == Discovery and Excavation == On March 18, 1935, a local resident discovered a mirror, bronze arrowheads, a bronze bell, and iron swords while digging up tree roots. A field survey was conducted on March 20, followed by a full excavation and mapping of the tumulus in January 1936. In 1960, another excavation and mapping took place, leading to new interpretations of the kofun's type. In 2016, a re-evaluation suggested that it may have been a {{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōhō-chūen Kofun}}. Today, a reconstructed mound is preserved inside Shindo Otsukayama Park. == location == Shindo Otsukayama Kofun was built on a sand dune ridge along {{ill|Sagami Bay|en|Sagami Bay|WD=Q1061221|lt=Sagami Bay}}. At the time of excavation, the tumulus sat 19.5 meters above sea level, 11 meters higher than nearby rice fields, making it the highest point in the surrounding lowland. Because it was built on sand dunes, early researchers nicknamed it "the sand dune tumulus". The surrounding land was not highly fertile, and no large settlements were found nearby. However, the kofun’s strategic location near both Sagami Bay and the Sagami River mouth suggests that it was constructed as a major landmark on a transportation route. == Structure == The mound was never fully excavated, and its exact type remains unknown. Based on surveys, three different hypotheses have been proposed: 1. Keyhole-shaped tumulus ({{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun}}) 2. Rectangular-front tumulus ({{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoho-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}) 3. Double middle-round tumulus ({{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōhō-chūen Kofun|qq=}}) Since the mound was destroyed before its structure could be confirmed, the exact type will never be known. === Surface Features === * Stone covering (Fuki-ishi) ** A 1960 excavation discovered fist-sized stones at the mound’s summit, suggesting a stone covering may have existed. ** However, 1936 excavation records make no mention of it, making this uncertain. * Stepped construction (Dan-chiku) ** No evidence was found. * Haniwa (ceramic tomb markers) ** None were discovered. * Moat (Shuchu-kyokusen) ** No moat was found. The burial chambers were located 0.75–0.8 meters underground for the clay chamber burial, and 1.3 meters underground for the wooden coffin burial. == burial goods == [[File:真土大塚山古墳出土 三角縁四神二獣鏡 (J-23148).JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Sankakuen Shijin Nijukyo mirror}}{{small|On display at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|en|Tokyo National Museum|WD=Q653433|lt=Tokyo National Museum}}.}}]] burial goods from both burials include: === Wooden Coffin Burial === Discovered before World War II, these items are housed in the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|en|Tokyo National Museum|WD=Q653433|lt=Tokyo National Museum}}: * 1 {{ill|Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|ja|三角縁神獣鏡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror) ** Identical to a mirror found in the {{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|en|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|WD=Q11540994|lt=Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun}} (Kyoto), indicating a connection to the Yamato region. * Multiple {{ill|Kudatama|ja|管玉|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kudatama}} (tube beads) and circular bronze ornaments * 39 bronze arrowheads * 2 iron axes * 1 sword fragment * 1 knife fragment * Pottery fragments ** Believed to date from the late Yayoi period to the early Kofun period. === Clay Chamber Burial === Excavated after World War II, these items are housed in the {{ill|Hiratsuka City Museum|ja|平塚市博物館|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiratsuka City Museum|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q104708570}}: * 1 Four Beast Mirror (変形四獣鏡) * 1 Crystal Magatama bead * 2 Crystal "abacus" beads * 150 glass beads * 1 bronze arrowhead * 3 bronze bells * 1 spear-plane (槍鉋, yari-ganna) * Pottery fragments ** Dated to the late Yayoi period or early Kofun period. File:真土大塚山古墳出土 銅鏃.JPG|Bronze arrowheads
{{small|On display at the Matsudo City Museum.}} == Historical Significance == Although the mound itself was lost, burial goods confirm that the person buried here had strong ties to the Yamato court. The kofun was likely built between the late 3rd century and mid-4th century, or possibly in the late 4th century. It fills a chronological gap between the {{ill|Akibayama Kofun Cluster|en|Akibayama Kofun Cluster|WD=Q11595836|lt=Akibayama Kofun Cluster}} and the {{ill|Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|en|Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|WD=Q11653084|lt=Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster}}. Its location near the Sagami River suggests a close connection to marine trade routes, particularly with the Nagara Sakurayama Kofun Group. Some scholars believe the tumulus was built by the Sōbu Kuni no Miyatsuko (相武国造), while others argue that the Shinaga Kuni no Miyatsuko (師長国造) controlled this region.[https://www.hirahaku.jp/hakubutsukan_archive/kouko/00000035/2.html Hiratsuka City Museum] == Historic Site == === Hiratsuka City Designated Cultural Property === * Important Cultural Property (Tangible Cultural Property) ** "Shindo Otsukayama Kofun burial goods" (designation1 February 1, 2010).[http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/bunka/page-c_01316.html Hiratsuka City Cultural Property Database] == References == == External Links == * [http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/zukan/iseki/iseki_03.htm Hiratsuka City Archaeological Records] * Double middle-round tumulus ({{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōhō-chūen Kofun|qq=}}) Since the mound was destroyed before its structure could be confirmed, the exact type will never be known. === Surface Features === * Stone covering (Fuki-ishi) ** A 1960 excavation discovered fist-sized stones at the mound’s summit, suggesting a stone covering may have existed. ** However, 1936 excavation records make no mention of it, making this uncertain. * Stepped construction (Dan-chiku) ** No evidence was found. * Haniwa (ceramic tomb markers) ** None were discovered. * Moat (Shuchu-kyokusen) ** No moat was found. The burial chambers were located 0.75–0.8 meters underground for the clay chamber burial, and 1.3 meters underground for the wooden coffin burial. == burial goods == [[File:真土大塚山古墳出土 三角縁四神二獣鏡 (J-23148).JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Sankakuen Shijin Nijukyo mirror}}{{small|On display at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|en|Tokyo National Museum|WD=Q653433|lt=Tokyo National Museum}}.}}]] burial goods from both burials include: === Wooden Coffin Burial === Discovered before World War II, these items are housed in the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|en|Tokyo National Museum|WD=Q653433|lt=Tokyo National Museum}}: * 1 {{ill|Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|ja|三角縁神獣鏡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror) ** Identical to a mirror found in the {{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|en|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|WD=Q11540994|lt=Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun}} (Kyoto), indicating a connection to the Yamato region. * Multiple {{ill|Kudatama|ja|管玉|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kudatama}} (tube beads) and circular bronze ornaments * 39 bronze arrowheads * 2 iron axes * 1 sword fragment * 1 knife fragment * Pottery fragments ** Believed to date from the late Yayoi period to the early Kofun period. === Clay Chamber Burial === Excavated after World War II, these items are housed in the {{ill|Hiratsuka City Museum|ja|平塚市博物館|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiratsuka City Museum|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q104708570}}: * 1 Four Beast Mirror (変形四獣鏡) * 1 Crystal Magatama bead * 2 Crystal "abacus" beads * 150 glass beads * 1 bronze arrowhead * 3 bronze bells * 1 spear-plane (槍鉋, yari-ganna) * Pottery fragments ** Dated to the late Yayoi period or early Kofun period. File:真土大塚山古墳出土 銅鏃.JPG|Bronze arrowheads
{{small|On display at the Matsudo City Museum.}} == Historical Significance == Although the mound itself was lost, burial goods confirm that the person buried here had strong ties to the Yamato court. The kofun was likely built between the late 3rd century and mid-4th century, or possibly in the late 4th century. It fills a chronological gap between the {{ill|Akibayama Kofun Cluster|en|Akibayama Kofun Cluster|WD=Q11595836|lt=Akibayama Kofun Cluster}} and the {{ill|Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|en|Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|WD=Q11653084|lt=Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster}}. Its location near the Sagami River suggests a close connection to marine trade routes, particularly with the Nagara Sakurayama Kofun Group. Some scholars believe the tumulus was built by the Sōbu Kuni no Miyatsuko (相武国造), while others argue that the Shinaga Kuni no Miyatsuko (師長国造) controlled this region.[https://www.hirahaku.jp/hakubutsukan_archive/kouko/00000035/2.html Hiratsuka City Museum] == Historic Site == === Hiratsuka City Designated Cultural Property === * Important Cultural Property (Tangible Cultural Property) ** "Shindo Otsukayama Kofun burial goods" (designation1 February 1, 2010).[http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/bunka/page-c_01316.html Hiratsuka City Cultural Property Reconstructed mound in Shindo Otsukayama Park | architectural_styles= {{ill|Q11410445|WD=Q11410445|1=Sōhō-chūen Kofun}} }} {{ill|Shindo Otsukayama Kofun|ja|真土大塚山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shindo Otsukayama Kofun}} was an ancient Kofun located in {{ill|Hiratsuka|en|Hiratsuka|WD=Q502199|lt=Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|1=Hiratsuka}}, Japan. The site is now lost, but burial goods from the burial have been designation1 as an Important Cultural Property of Hiratsuka City. The original type of the tumulus is debated, with three competing theories: 1. {{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōhō-chūen Kofun}} (double middle-round tumulus) 2. {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}} (keyhole-shaped tumulus) 3. {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=enwiki is a redirect|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun}} (rectangular-front tumulus) However, no excavation was conducted before the mound was destroyed, making its true form uncertain. == Discovery and Excavation == On March 18, 1935, a local resident discovered a mirror, bronze arrowheads, a bronze bell, and iron swords while digging up tree roots. A field survey was conducted on March 20, followed by a full excavation and mapping of the tumulus in January 1936. In 1960, another excavation and mapping took place, leading to new interpretations of the kofun's type. In 2016, a re-evaluation suggested that it may have been a {{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōhō-chūen Kofun}}. Today, a reconstructed mound is preserved inside Shindo Otsukayama Park. == location == Shindo Otsukayama Kofun was built on a sand dune ridge along {{ill|Sagami Bay|en|Sagami Bay|WD=Q1061221|lt=Sagami Bay|1=Sagami Bay}}. At the time of excavation, the tumulus sat 19.5 meters above sea level, 11 meters higher than nearby rice fields, making it the highest point in the surrounding lowland. Because it was built on sand dunes, early researchers nicknamed it "the sand dune tumulus". The surrounding land was not highly fertile, and no large settlements were found nearby. However, the kofun’s strategic location near both Sagami Bay and the Sagami River mouth suggests that it was constructed as a major landmark on a transportation route. == Structure == The mound was never fully excavated, and its exact type remains unknown. Based on surveys, three different hypotheses have been proposed: 1. Keyhole-shaped tumulus ({{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}}) 2. Rectangular-front tumulus ({{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoho-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}) 3. Double middle-round tumulus ({{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōhō-chūen Kofun|qq=}}) Since the mound was destroyed before its structure could be confirmed, the exact type will never be known. === Surface Features === * Stone covering (Fuki-ishi) ** A 1960 excavation discovered fist-sized stones at the mound’s summit, suggesting a stone covering may have existed. ** However, 1936 excavation records make no mention of it, making this uncertain. * Stepped construction (Dan-chiku) ** No evidence was found. * Haniwa (ceramic tomb markers) ** None were discovered. * Moat (Shuchu-kyokusen) ** No moat was found. The burial chambers were located 0.75–0.8 meters underground for the clay chamber burial, and 1.3 meters underground for the wooden coffin burial. == burial goods == [[File:真土大塚山古墳出土 三角縁四神二獣鏡 (J-23148).JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Sankakuen Shijin Nijukyo mirror}}{{small|On display at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|en|Tokyo National Museum|WD=Q653433|lt=Tokyo National Museum|1=Tokyo National Museum}}.}}]] burial goods from both burials include: === Wooden Coffin Burial === Discovered before World War II, these items are housed in the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|en|Tokyo National Museum|WD=Q653433|lt=Tokyo National Museum|1=Tokyo National Museum}}: * 1 {{ill|Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|ja|三角縁神獣鏡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror) ** Identical to a mirror found in the {{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|en|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|WD=Q11540994|lt=Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|1=Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun}} (Kyoto), indicating a connection to the Yamato region. * Multiple {{ill|Kudatama|ja|管玉|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kudatama}} (tube beads) and circular bronze ornaments * 39 bronze arrowheads * 2 iron axes * 1 sword fragment * 1 knife fragment * Pottery fragments ** Believed to date from the late Yayoi period to the early Kofun period. === Clay Chamber Burial === Excavated after World War II, these items are housed in the {{ill|Hiratsuka City Museum|ja|平塚市博物館|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiratsuka City Museum|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q104708570|1=Hiratsuka City Museum}}: * 1 Four Beast Mirror (変形四獣鏡) * 1 Crystal Magatama bead * 2 Crystal "abacus" beads * 150 glass beads * 1 bronze arrowhead * 3 bronze bells * 1 spear-plane (槍鉋, yari-ganna) * Pottery fragments ** Dated to the late Yayoi period or early Kofun period. It fills a chronological gap between the {{ill|Akibayama Kofun Cluster|en|Akibayama Kofun Cluster|WD=Q11595836|lt=Akibayama Kofun Cluster|1=Akibayama Kofun Cluster}} and the {{ill|Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|en|Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|WD=Q11653084|lt=Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|1=Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster}}. [[co:commons:Category:Shindo Otsukayama Kofun]][[ja:真土大塚山古墳]] [[co:commons:Category:Shindo Otsukayama Kofun]][[ja:真土大塚山古墳]] [[Category:sn_crud|TESTcommons:Category:Shindo Otsukayama Kofun]][[ja:真土大塚山古墳]] {{Infobox ancient site | name = Shindo Otsukayama Kofun | native_name = 真土大塚山古墳 | location = {{ill|Hiratsuka|en|Hiratsuka|WD=Q502199|lt=Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|1=Hiratsuka}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|en|Kanagawa Prefecture|WD=Q127513|lt=Kanagawa Prefecture|1=Kanagawa Prefecture}}, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|35.358722|N|139.348556|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōhō-chūen Kofun|qq=}} / {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}} / {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoho-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} | length = Unknown | built = Late 3rd century - Mid 4th century (or late 4th century) | burial = Wooden coffin burial, {{ill|Nendo-kaku|ja|粘土槨|1=Clay coffin chamber|1=Clay coffin chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nendo-kaku|13=User:Immanuelle/Clay coffin chamber|qq=}} (clay chamber) | burial goods = {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡|1=Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sankakuen shinjukyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|qq=}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror), weapons, jewelry | designation1 = None | map = Japan Kanagawa | map_caption = location in Kanagawa Prefecture | image = [[File:Shindo Otsukayama Kofun, funkyu.jpg|280px]]
Reconstructed mound in Shindo Otsukayama Park | architectural_styles= {{ill|Q11410445|WD=Q11410445|1=Sōhō-chūen Kofun}} }} {{ill|Shindo Otsukayama Kofun|ja|真土大塚山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shindo Otsukayama Kofun}} was an ancient Kofun located in {{ill|Hiratsuka|en|Hiratsuka|WD=Q502199|lt=Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|1=Hiratsuka}}, Japan. The site is now lost, but burial goods from the burial have been designation1 as an Important Cultural Property of Hiratsuka City. The original type of the tumulus is debated, with three competing theories: 1. {{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōhō-chūen Kofun}} (double middle-round tumulus) 2. {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}} (keyhole-shaped tumulus) 3. {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=enwiki is a redirect|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun}} (rectangular-front tumulus) However, no excavation was conducted before the mound was destroyed, making its true form uncertain. == Discovery and Excavation == On March 18, 1935, a local resident discovered a mirror, bronze arrowheads, a bronze bell, and iron swords while digging up tree roots. A field survey was conducted on March 20, followed by a full excavation and mapping of the tumulus in January 1936. In 1960, another excavation and mapping took place, leading to new interpretations of the kofun's type. In 2016, a re-evaluation suggested that it may have been a {{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōhō-chūen Kofun}}. Today, a reconstructed mound is preserved inside Shindo Otsukayama Park. == location == Shindo Otsukayama Kofun was built on a sand dune ridge along {{ill|Sagami Bay|en|Sagami Bay|WD=Q1061221|lt=Sagami Bay|1=Sagami Bay}}. At the time of excavation, the tumulus sat 19.5 meters above sea level, 11 meters higher than nearby rice fields, making it the highest point in the surrounding lowland. Because it was built on sand dunes, early researchers nicknamed it "the sand dune tumulus". The surrounding land was not highly fertile, and no large settlements were found nearby. However, the kofun’s strategic location near both Sagami Bay and the Sagami River mouth suggests that it was constructed as a major landmark on a transportation route. == Structure == The mound was never fully excavated, and its exact type remains unknown. Based on surveys, three different hypotheses have been proposed: 1. Keyhole-shaped tumulus ({{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}}) 2. Rectangular-front tumulus ({{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoho-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}) 3. Double middle-round tumulus ({{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōhō-chūen Kofun|qq=}}) Since the mound was destroyed before its structure could be confirmed, the exact type will never be known. === Surface Features === * Stone covering (Fuki-ishi) ** A 1960 excavation discovered fist-sized stones at the mound’s summit, suggesting a stone covering may have existed. ** However, 1936 excavation records make no mention of it, making this uncertain. * Stepped construction (Dan-chiku) ** No evidence was found. * Haniwa (ceramic tomb markers) ** None were discovered. * Moat (Shuchu-kyokusen) ** No moat was found. The burial chambers were located 0.75–0.8 meters underground for the clay chamber burial, and 1.3 meters underground for the wooden coffin burial. == burial goods == [[File:真土大塚山古墳出土 三角縁四神二獣鏡 (J-23148).JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Sankakuen Shijin Nijukyo mirror}}{{small|On display at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|en|Tokyo National Museum|WD=Q653433|lt=Tokyo National Museum|1=Tokyo National Museum}}.}}]] burial goods from both burials include: === Wooden Coffin Burial === Discovered before World War II, these items are housed in the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|en|Tokyo National Museum|WD=Q653433|lt=Tokyo National Museum|1=Tokyo National Museum}}: * 1 {{ill|Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|ja|三角縁神獣鏡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror) ** Identical to a mirror found in the {{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|en|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|WD=Q11540994|lt=Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|1=Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun}} (Kyoto), indicating a connection to the Yamato region. * Multiple {{ill|Kudatama|ja|管玉|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kudatama}} (tube beads) and circular bronze ornaments * 39 bronze arrowheads * 2 iron axes * 1 sword fragment * 1 knife fragment * Pottery fragments ** Believed to date from the late Yayoi period to the early Kofun period. === Clay Chamber Burial === Excavated after World War II, these items are housed in the {{ill|Hiratsuka City Museum|ja|平塚市博物館|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiratsuka City Museum|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q104708570|1=Hiratsuka City Museum}}: * 1 Four Beast Mirror (変形四獣鏡) * 1 Crystal Magatama bead * 2 Crystal "abacus" beads * 150 glass beads * 1 bronze arrowhead * 3 bronze bells * 1 spear-plane (槍鉋, yari-ganna) * Pottery fragments ** Dated to the late Yayoi period or early Kofun period. File:真土大塚山古墳出土 銅鏃.JPG|Bronze arrowheads
{{small|On display at the Matsudo City Museum.}} == Historical Significance == Although the mound itself was lost, burial goods confirm that the person buried here had strong ties to the Yamato court. The kofun was likely built between the late 3rd century and mid-4th century, or possibly in the late 4th century. It fills a chronological gap between the {{ill|Akibayama Kofun Cluster|en|Akibayama Kofun Cluster|WD=Q11595836|lt=Akibayama Kofun Cluster|1=Akibayama Kofun Cluster}} and the {{ill|Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|en|Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|WD=Q11653084|lt=Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|1=Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster}}. Its location near the Sagami River suggests a close connection to marine trade routes, particularly with the Nagara Sakurayama Kofun Group. Some scholars believe the tumulus was built by the Sōbu Kuni no Miyatsuko (相武国造), while others argue that the Shinaga Kuni no Miyatsuko (師長国造) controlled this region.[https://www.hirahaku.jp/hakubutsukan_archive/kouko/00000035/2.html Hiratsuka City Museum] == Historic Site == === Hiratsuka City Designated Cultural Property === * Important Cultural Property (Tangible Cultural Property) ** "Shindo Otsukayama Kofun burial goods" (designation1 February 1, 2010).[http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/bunka/page-c_01316.html Hiratsuka City Cultural Property [[co:commons:Category:Shindo Otsukayama Kofun]][[ja:真土大塚山古墳]] [[co:commons:Category:Shindo Otsukayama Kofun]][[ja:真土大塚山古墳]] [[Category:sn_crud|TESTcommons:Category:Shindo Otsukayama Kofun]][[ja:真土大塚山古墳]] {{Infobox ancient site | name = Shindo Otsukayama Kofun | native_name = 真土大塚山古墳 | location = {{ill|Hiratsuka|en|Hiratsuka|WD=Q502199|lt=Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|1=Hiratsuka}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|en|Kanagawa Prefecture|WD=Q127513|lt=Kanagawa Prefecture|1=Kanagawa Prefecture}}, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|35.358722|N|139.348556|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōhō-chūen Kofun|qq=}} / {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}} / {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoho-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} | length = Unknown | built = Late 3rd century - Mid 4th century (or late 4th century) | burial = Wooden coffin burial, {{ill|Nendo-kaku|ja|粘土槨|1=Clay coffin chamber|1=Clay coffin chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nendo-kaku|13=User:Immanuelle/Clay coffin chamber|qq=}} (clay chamber) | burial goods = {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡|1=Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sankakuen shinjukyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|qq=}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror), weapons, jewelry | designation1 = None | map = Japan Kanagawa | map_caption = location in Kanagawa Prefecture | image = [[File:Shindo Otsukayama Kofun, funkyu.jpg|280px]]
Reconstructed mound in Shindo Otsukayama Park | architectural_styles= {{ill|Q11410445|WD=Q11410445|1=Sōhō-chūen Kofun}} }} {{ill|Shindo Otsukayama Kofun|ja|真土大塚山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shindo Otsukayama Kofun}} was an ancient Kofun located in {{ill|Hiratsuka|en|Hiratsuka|WD=Q502199|lt=Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|1=Hiratsuka}}, Japan. The site is now lost, but burial goods from the burial have been designation1 as an Important Cultural Property of Hiratsuka City. The original type of the tumulus is debated, with three competing theories: 1. {{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōhō-chūen Kofun}} (double middle-round tumulus) 2. {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}} (keyhole-shaped tumulus) 3. {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=enwiki is a redirect|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun}} (rectangular-front tumulus) However, no excavation was conducted before the mound was destroyed, making its true form uncertain. == Discovery and Excavation == On March 18, 1935, a local resident discovered a mirror, bronze arrowheads, a bronze bell, and iron swords while digging up tree roots. A field survey was conducted on March 20, followed by a full excavation and mapping of the tumulus in January 1936. In 1960, another excavation and mapping took place, leading to new interpretations of the kofun's type. In 2016, a re-evaluation suggested that it may have been a {{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōhō-chūen Kofun}}. Today, a reconstructed mound is preserved inside Shindo Otsukayama Park. == location == Shindo Otsukayama Kofun was built on a sand dune ridge along {{ill|Sagami Bay|en|Sagami Bay|WD=Q1061221|lt=Sagami Bay|1=Sagami Bay}}. At the time of excavation, the tumulus sat 19.5 meters above sea level, 11 meters higher than nearby rice fields, making it the highest point in the surrounding lowland. Because it was built on sand dunes, early researchers nicknamed it "the sand dune tumulus". The surrounding land was not highly fertile, and no large settlements were found nearby. However, the kofun’s strategic location near both Sagami Bay and the Sagami River mouth suggests that it was constructed as a major landmark on a transportation route. == Structure == The mound was never fully excavated, and its exact type remains unknown. Based on surveys, three different hypotheses have been proposed: 1. Keyhole-shaped tumulus ({{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}}) 2. Rectangular-front tumulus ({{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoho-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}) 3. Double middle-round tumulus ({{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōhō-chūen Kofun|qq=}}) Since the mound was destroyed before its structure could be confirmed, the exact type will never be known. === Surface Features === * Stone covering (Fuki-ishi) ** A 1960 excavation discovered fist-sized stones at the mound’s summit, suggesting a stone covering may have existed. ** However, 1936 excavation records make no mention of it, making this uncertain. * Stepped construction (Dan-chiku) ** No evidence was found. * Haniwa (ceramic tomb markers) ** None were discovered. * Moat (Shuchu-kyokusen) ** No moat was found. The burial chambers were located 0.75–0.8 meters underground for the clay chamber burial, and 1.3 meters underground for the wooden coffin burial. == burial goods == [[File:真土大塚山古墳出土 三角縁四神二獣鏡 (J-23148).JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Sankakuen Shijin Nijukyo mirror}}{{small|On display at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|en|Tokyo National Museum|WD=Q653433|lt=Tokyo National Museum|1=Tokyo National Museum}}.}}]] burial goods from both burials include: === Wooden Coffin Burial === Discovered before World War II, these items are housed in the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|en|Tokyo National Museum|WD=Q653433|lt=Tokyo National Museum|1=Tokyo National Museum}}: * 1 {{ill|Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|ja|三角縁神獣鏡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror) ** Identical to a mirror found in the {{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|en|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|WD=Q11540994|lt=Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|1=Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun}} (Kyoto), indicating a connection to the Yamato region. * Multiple {{ill|Kudatama|ja|管玉|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kudatama}} (tube beads) and circular bronze ornaments * 39 bronze arrowheads * 2 iron axes * 1 sword fragment * 1 knife fragment * Pottery fragments ** Believed to date from the late Yayoi period to the early Kofun period. === Clay Chamber Burial === Excavated after World War II, these items are housed in the {{ill|Hiratsuka City Museum|ja|平塚市博物館|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiratsuka City Museum|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q104708570|1=Hiratsuka City Museum}}: * 1 Four Beast Mirror (変形四獣鏡) * 1 Crystal Magatama bead * 2 Crystal "abacus" beads * 150 glass beads * 1 bronze arrowhead * 3 bronze bells * 1 spear-plane (槍鉋, yari-ganna) * Pottery fragments ** Dated to the late Yayoi period or early Kofun period. File:真土大塚山古墳出土 銅鏃.JPG|Bronze arrowheads
{{small|On display at the Matsudo City Museum.}} == Historical Significance == Although the mound itself was lost, burial goods confirm that the person buried here had strong ties to the Yamato court. The kofun was likely built between the late 3rd century and mid-4th century, or possibly in the late 4th century. It fills a chronological gap between the {{ill|Akibayama Kofun Cluster|en|Akibayama Kofun Cluster|WD=Q11595836|lt=Akibayama Kofun Cluster|1=Akibayama Kofun Cluster}} and the {{ill|Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|en|Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|WD=Q11653084|lt=Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|1=Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster}}. Its location near the Sagami River suggests a close connection to marine trade routes, particularly with the Nagara Sakurayama Kofun Group. Some scholars believe the tumulus was built by the Sōbu Kuni no Miyatsuko (相武国造), while others argue that the Shinaga Kuni no Miyatsuko (師長国造) controlled this region.[https://www.hirahaku.jp/hakubutsukan_archive/kouko/00000035/2.html Hiratsuka City Museum] == Historic Site == === Hiratsuka City Designated Cultural Property === * Important Cultural Property (Tangible Cultural Property) ** "Shindo Otsukayama Kofun burial goods" (designation1 February 1, 2010).[http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/bunka/page-c_01316.html Hiratsuka City Cultural Property Rectangular-front tumulus ({{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoho-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}) 3. Double middle-round tumulus ({{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōhō-chūen Kofun|qq=}}) Since the mound was destroyed before its structure could be confirmed, the exact type will never be known. === Surface Features === * Stone covering (Fuki-ishi) ** A 1960 excavation discovered fist-sized stones at the mound’s summit, suggesting a stone covering may have existed. ** However, 1936 excavation records make no mention of it, making this uncertain. * Stepped construction (Dan-chiku) ** No evidence was found. * Haniwa (ceramic tomb markers) ** None were discovered. * Moat (Shuchu-kyokusen) ** No moat was found. The burial chambers were located 0.75–0.8 meters underground for the clay chamber burial, and 1.3 meters underground for the wooden coffin burial. == burial goods == [[File:真土大塚山古墳出土 三角縁四神二獣鏡 (J-23148).JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Sankakuen Shijin Nijukyo mirror}}{{small|On display at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|en|Tokyo National Museum|WD=Q653433|lt=Tokyo National Museum|1=Tokyo National Museum}}.}}]] burial goods from both burials include: === Wooden Coffin Burial === Discovered before World War II, these items are housed in the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|en|Tokyo National Museum|WD=Q653433|lt=Tokyo National Museum|1=Tokyo National Museum}}: * 1 {{ill|Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|ja|三角縁神獣鏡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror) ** Identical to a mirror found in the {{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|en|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|WD=Q11540994|lt=Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|1=Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun}} (Kyoto), indicating a connection to the Yamato region. * Multiple {{ill|Kudatama|ja|管玉|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kudatama}} (tube beads) and circular bronze ornaments * 39 bronze arrowheads * 2 iron axes * 1 sword fragment * 1 knife fragment * Pottery fragments ** Believed to date from the late Yayoi period to the early Kofun period. === Clay Chamber Burial === Excavated after World War II, these items are housed in the {{ill|Hiratsuka City Museum|ja|平塚市博物館|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiratsuka City Museum|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q104708570|1=Hiratsuka City Museum}}: * 1 Four Beast Mirror (変形四獣鏡) * 1 Crystal Magatama bead * 2 Crystal "abacus" beads * 150 glass beads * 1 bronze arrowhead * 3 bronze bells * 1 spear-plane (槍鉋, yari-ganna) * Pottery fragments ** Dated to the late Yayoi period or early Kofun period. File:真土大塚山古墳出土 銅鏃.JPG|Bronze arrowheads
{{small|On display at the Matsudo City Museum.}} == Historical Significance == Although the mound itself was lost, burial goods confirm that the person buried here had strong ties to the Yamato court. The kofun was likely built between the late 3rd century and mid-4th century, or possibly in the late 4th century. It fills a chronological gap between the {{ill|Akibayama Kofun Cluster|en|Akibayama Kofun Cluster|WD=Q11595836|lt=Akibayama Kofun Cluster|1=Akibayama Kofun Cluster}} and the {{ill|Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|en|Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|WD=Q11653084|lt=Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|1=Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster}}. Its location near the Sagami River suggests a close connection to marine trade routes, particularly with the Nagara Sakurayama Kofun Group. Some scholars believe the tumulus was built by the Sōbu Kuni no Miyatsuko (相武国造), while others argue that the Shinaga Kuni no Miyatsuko (師長国造) controlled this region.[https://www.hirahaku.jp/hakubutsukan_archive/kouko/00000035/2.html Hiratsuka City Museum] == Historic Site == === Hiratsuka City Designated Cultural Property === * Important Cultural Property (Tangible Cultural Property) ** "Shindo Otsukayama Kofun burial goods" (designation1 February 1, 2010).[http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/bunka/page-c_01316.html Hiratsuka City Cultural Property Reconstructed mound in Shindo Otsukayama Park | architectural_styles= {{ill|Q11410445|WD=Q11410445|1=Sōhō-chūen Kofun}} }} {{ill|Shindo Otsukayama Kofun|ja|真土大塚山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shindo Otsukayama Kofun}} was an ancient Kofun located in {{ill|Hiratsuka|en|Hiratsuka|WD=Q502199|lt=Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|1=Hiratsuka}}, Japan. The site is now lost, but burial goods from the burial have been designation1 as an Important Cultural Property of Hiratsuka City. The original type of the tumulus is debated, with three competing theories: 1. {{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōhō-chūen Kofun}} (double middle-round tumulus) 2. {{ill|Zenpōkōenfun|en|Zenpōkōenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpōkōenfun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}} (keyhole-shaped tumulus) 3. {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=enwiki is a redirect|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun}} (rectangular-front tumulus) However, no excavation was conducted before the mound was destroyed, making its true form uncertain. == Discovery and Excavation == On March 18, 1935, a local resident discovered a mirror, bronze arrowheads, a bronze bell, and iron swords while digging up tree roots. A field survey was conducted on March 20, followed by a full excavation and mapping of the tumulus in January 1936. In 1960, another excavation and mapping took place, leading to new interpretations of the kofun's type. In 2016, a re-evaluation suggested that it may have been a {{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōhō-chūen Kofun}}. Today, a reconstructed mound is preserved inside Shindo Otsukayama Park. == location == Shindo Otsukayama Kofun was built on a sand dune ridge along {{ill|Sagami Bay|en|Sagami Bay|WD=Q1061221|lt=Sagami Bay|1=Sagami Bay}}. At the time of excavation, the tumulus sat 19.5 meters above sea level, 11 meters higher than nearby rice fields, making it the highest point in the surrounding lowland. Because it was built on sand dunes, early researchers nicknamed it "the sand dune tumulus". The surrounding land was not highly fertile, and no large settlements were found nearby. However, the kofun’s strategic location near both Sagami Bay and the Sagami River mouth suggests that it was constructed as a major landmark on a transportation route. == Structure == The mound was never fully excavated, and its exact type remains unknown. [[co:commons:Category:Shindo Otsukayama Kofun]][[ja:真土大塚山古墳]] [[co:commons:Category:Shindo Otsukayama Kofun]][[ja:真土大塚山古墳]] [[ja:真土大塚山古墳]] {{Infobox ancient site | name = Shindo Otsukayama Kofun | native_name = 真土大塚山古墳 | location = {{ill|Hiratsuka|en|Hiratsuka|WD=Q502199|lt=Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|1=Hiratsuka}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|en|Kanagawa Prefecture|WD=Q127513|lt=Kanagawa Prefecture|1=Kanagawa Prefecture}}, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|35.358722|N|139.348556|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | region = Japan | type = {{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōhō-chūen Kofun|qq=}} / {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|en|Zenpō-kōen-fun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpō-kōen-fun|1=Zenpō-kōen-fun}} / {{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoho-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} | length = Unknown | built = Late 3rd century - Mid 4th century (or late 4th century) | burial = Wooden coffin burial, {{ill|Nendo-kaku|ja|粘土槨|1=Clay coffin chamber|1=Clay coffin chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nendo-kaku|13=User:Immanuelle/Clay coffin chamber|qq=}} (clay chamber) | burial goods = {{ill|Sankakuen shinjukyo|ja|三角縁神獣鏡|1=Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sankakuen shinjukyo|13=User:Immanuelle/Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|qq=}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror), weapons, jewelry | designation1 = None | map = Japan Kanagawa | map_caption = location in Kanagawa Prefecture | image = [[File:Shindo Otsukayama Kofun, funkyu.jpg|280px]]
Reconstructed mound in Shindo Otsukayama Park | architectural_styles= {{ill|Q11410445|WD=Q11410445|1=Sōhō-chūen Kofun}} }} {{ill|Shindo Otsukayama Kofun|ja|真土大塚山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shindo Otsukayama Kofun}} was an ancient Kofun located in {{ill|Hiratsuka|en|Hiratsuka|WD=Q502199|lt=Hiratsuka, Kanagawa|1=Hiratsuka}}, Japan. The site is now lost, but burial goods from the burial have been designation1 as an Important Cultural Property of Hiratsuka City. The original type of the tumulus is debated, with three competing theories: 1. {{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōhō-chūen Kofun}} (double middle-round tumulus) 2. {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|en|Zenpō-kōen-fun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpō-kōen-fun|1=Zenpō-kōen-fun}} (keyhole-shaped tumulus) 3. {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=enwiki is a redirect|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun}} (rectangular-front tumulus) However, no excavation was conducted before the mound was destroyed, making its true form uncertain. == Discovery and Excavation == On March 18, 1935, a local resident discovered a mirror, bronze arrowheads, a bronze bell, and iron swords while digging up tree roots. A field survey was conducted on March 20, followed by a full excavation and mapping of the tumulus in January 1936. In 1960, another excavation and mapping took place, leading to new interpretations of the kofun's type. In 2016, a re-evaluation suggested that it may have been a {{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōhō-chūen Kofun}}. Today, a reconstructed mound is preserved inside Shindo Otsukayama Park. == location == Shindo Otsukayama Kofun was built on a sand dune ridge along {{ill|Sagami Bay|en|Sagami Bay|WD=Q1061221|lt=Sagami Bay|1=Sagami Bay}}. At the time of excavation, the tumulus sat 19.5 meters above sea level, 11 meters higher than nearby rice fields, making it the highest point in the surrounding lowland. Because it was built on sand dunes, early researchers nicknamed it "the sand dune tumulus". The surrounding land was not highly fertile, and no large settlements were found nearby. However, the kofun’s strategic location near both Sagami Bay and the Sagami River mouth suggests that it was constructed as a major landmark on a transportation route. == Structure == The mound was never fully excavated, and its exact type remains unknown. Based on surveys, three different hypotheses have been proposed: 1. Keyhole-shaped tumulus ({{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|en|Zenpō-kōen-fun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpō-kōen-fun|1=Zenpō-kōen-fun}}) 2. Rectangular-front tumulus ({{ill|Zenpokoho-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|1=Zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=zenpō-kōhō-fun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoho-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōhō-fun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}) 3. Double middle-round tumulus ({{ill|Sōhō-chūen Kofun|ja|双方中円墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōhō-chūen Kofun|qq=}}) Since the mound was destroyed before its structure could be confirmed, the exact type will never be known. === Surface Features === * Stone covering (Fuki-ishi) ** A 1960 excavation discovered fist-sized stones at the mound’s summit, suggesting a stone covering may have existed. ** However, 1936 excavation records make no mention of it, making this uncertain. * Stepped construction (Dan-chiku) ** No evidence was found. * Haniwa (ceramic tomb markers) ** None were discovered. * Moat (Shuchu-kyokusen) ** No moat was found. The burial chambers were located 0.75–0.8 meters underground for the clay chamber burial, and 1.3 meters underground for the wooden coffin burial. == burial goods == [[File:真土大塚山古墳出土 三角縁四神二獣鏡 (J-23148).JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Sankakuen Shijin Nijukyo mirror}}{{small|On display at the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|en|Tokyo National Museum|WD=Q653433|lt=Tokyo National Museum|1=Tokyo National Museum}}.}}]] burial goods from both burials include: === Wooden Coffin Burial === Discovered before World War II, these items are housed in the {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|en|Tokyo National Museum|WD=Q653433|lt=Tokyo National Museum|1=Tokyo National Museum}}: * 1 {{ill|Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|ja|三角縁神獣鏡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror}} (triangular-rimmed deity-beast mirror) ** Identical to a mirror found in the {{ill|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|en|Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|WD=Q11540994|lt=Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun|1=Tsubai Ōtsukayama Kofun}} (Kyoto), indicating a connection to the Yamato region. * Multiple {{ill|Kudatama|ja|管玉|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kudatama}} (tube beads) and circular bronze ornaments * 39 bronze arrowheads * 2 iron axes * 1 sword fragment * 1 knife fragment * Pottery fragments ** Believed to date from the late Yayoi period to the early Kofun period. === Clay Chamber Burial === Excavated after World War II, these items are housed in the {{ill|Hiratsuka City Museum|ja|平塚市博物館|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiratsuka City Museum|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q104708570|1=Hiratsuka City Museum}}: * 1 Four Beast Mirror (変形四獣鏡) * 1 Crystal Magatama bead * 2 Crystal "abacus" beads * 150 glass beads * 1 bronze arrowhead * 3 bronze bells * 1 spear-plane (槍鉋, yari-ganna) * Pottery fragments ** Dated to the late Yayoi period or early Kofun period. File:真土大塚山古墳出土 銅鏃.JPG|Bronze arrowheads
{{small|On display at the Matsudo City Museum.}} == Historical Significance == Although the mound itself was lost, burial goods confirm that the person buried here had strong ties to the Yamato court. The kofun was likely built between the late 3rd century and mid-4th century, or possibly in the late 4th century. It fills a chronological gap between the {{ill|Akibayama Kofun Cluster|en|Akibayama Kofun Cluster|WD=Q11595836|lt=Akibayama Kofun Cluster|1=Akibayama Kofun Cluster}} and the {{ill|Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|en|Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|WD=Q11653084|lt=Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster|1=Nagae-Sakurayama Kofun Cluster}}. Its location near the Sagami River suggests a close connection to marine trade routes, particularly with the Nagara Sakurayama Kofun Group. Some scholars believe the tumulus was built by the Sōbu Kuni no Miyatsuko (相武国造), while others argue that the Shinaga Kuni no Miyatsuko (師長国造) controlled this region.[https://www.hirahaku.jp/hakubutsukan_archive/kouko/00000035/2.html Hiratsuka City Museum] == Historic Site == === Hiratsuka City Designated Cultural Property === * Important Cultural Property (Tangible Cultural Property) ** "Shindo Otsukayama Kofun burial goods" (designation1 February 1, 2010).[http://www.city.hiratsuka.kanagawa.jp/bunka/page-c_01316.html Hiratsuka City Cultural Property
